# Varga Foundation documentation

> Open-source data and AI projects of the Varga Foundation.

This file contains all documentation content in a single document following the llmstxt.org standard.

## ADBC driver

Argus exposes an [Arrow ADBC](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/) surface (`libargus_adbc.so`) layered over its existing, validated ODBC stack. A query's result is returned as an Arrow **C Data Interface** stream of typed columns, so Arrow-native consumers (Power BI/Fabric's ADBC path, the Python/R ADBC bindings, DuckDB, etc.) get columnar data directly.

This anticipates the industry shift to ADBC — note what that shift is and is not: Power BI/Fabric is moving to ADBC by default and retiring the ODBC drivers it **embeds**, but Microsoft [states](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/transition-to-adbc) that the transition "doesn't change behavior for the ODBC connector when you use a separately installed ODBC driver". Argus is separately installed, so its ODBC path and its Power BI connector are unaffected; the ADBC surface is an addition, not a migration. See [BI tools](./bi-tools.md).

### Design

The driver is a thin Arrow adapter, not a reimplementation: a connection is an Argus ODBC connection (`SQLDriverConnect` with the usual `BACKEND=...;HOST=...` string), and `AdbcStatementExecuteQuery` runs the SQL through `SQLExecDirect`/`SQLFetch` and emits the rows as an `ArrowArrayStream`. Every backend, the streaming fetch and the native typed cells are reused unchanged.

The Arrow C Data Interface is a stable, dependency-free ABI, so the driver emits it **without linking any Arrow library**.

### Type mapping

| SQL type | Arrow type | C Data format |
|---|---|---|
| TINYINT/SMALLINT/INTEGER/BIGINT | int64 | `l` |
| REAL/FLOAT/DOUBLE | double | `g` |
| BIT | bool | `b` |
| DATE | date32 (days) | `tdD` |
| TIMESTAMP | timestamp, microseconds | `tsu:` |
| everything else (incl. DECIMAL) | utf8 | `u` |

DECIMAL stays utf8 to preserve arbitrary precision.

### Capabilities

- **ADBC 1.0.0 vtable** (`AdbcDriverInit`), so the driver loads via any ADBC driver manager by name.
- **Batched streaming**: the result statement stays open and each `get_next` pulls one Arrow batch (up to 4096 rows) lazily — memory is bounded regardless of result size.
- **Bound parameters** (`AdbcStatementBind`): the Arrow parameter array (row 0) is decoded and substituted into the query's `?` markers as SQL literals.
- **Metadata**: `AdbcConnectionGetTableSchema` (a table's columns as an Arrow schema, via `SQLColumns`), `AdbcConnectionGetTableTypes`, and `AdbcConnectionGetObjects` (the nested catalog/schema/table/column schema, with the catalog level populated; deeper levels are a follow-up).

### Usage

```c
#include "argus/adbc.h"

struct AdbcError err = {0};
struct AdbcDatabase db = {0};
AdbcDatabaseNew(&db, &err);
AdbcDatabaseSetOption(&db, "uri",
    "BACKEND=trino;HOST=trino;PORT=8080;UID=analyst;Database=tpch", &err);
AdbcDatabaseInit(&db, &err);

struct AdbcConnection conn = {0};
AdbcConnectionNew(&conn, &err);
AdbcConnectionInit(&conn, &db, &err);

struct AdbcStatement stmt = {0};
AdbcStatementNew(&conn, &stmt, &err);
AdbcStatementSetSqlQuery(&stmt, "SELECT * FROM tpch.tiny.nation", &err);

struct ArrowArrayStream stream = {0};
int64_t rows_affected = 0;
AdbcStatementExecuteQuery(&stmt, &stream, &rows_affected, &err);
/* consume `stream` with any Arrow C Data Interface importer */
```

### Building and testing

Built with `-DBUILD_ADBC=ON` (the default). The integration test (`tests/integration/test_adbc.cpp`) runs the whole surface against a live Trino and imports every result with Arrow C++'s own `ImportRecordBatchReader`/`ImportSchema` — the reference C Data Interface validator.

---

## BI tools

Which BI tools can reach Argus, what each one needs, and what Argus ships for it.

### The short version

Most BI tools need **nothing but the driver and a DSN**. Only two justify a packaged connector: Power BI (because generic ODBC cannot fold `LIMIT`/`TOP`) and Tableau (because a named connector fixes the SQL dialect and can be published). Everything else either speaks generic ODBC — in which case a correct driver is the whole answer — or does not speak ODBC at all.

| Tool | Speaks | Argus artifact | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Power BI Desktop / Service | ODBC via a custom connector | `Argus.mez` / `Argus.pqx` | shipped with each [release](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/argus/releases) |
| Tableau Desktop / Server | ODBC via a `.taco`, or generic ODBC | `argus-{trino,hive,impala,mysql,bigquery}.taco` | shipped |
| Tableau Cloud | ODBC **through Tableau Bridge only** | `.taco` + Bridge | limited — see below |
| Excel (Windows / Mac) | generic ODBC only | none possible | driver only |
| Qlik Sense (Windows) / QlikView | ODBC Connector Package | none needed | driver only |
| Qlik Sense SaaS | no ODBC | — | out of scope |
| Alteryx / MicroStrategy / SSIS / SSRS / SAS | generic ODBC | none needed | driver only |
| KNIME / Dataiku / Spotfire | ODBC or JDBC | none needed | driver only, via ODBC |
| DBeaver | JDBC only | — | out of scope |
| Apache Superset | SQLAlchemy | — | separate project |
| Metabase | JDBC driver plugin | — | separate project |
| Looker / Looker Studio / Amazon QuickSight | managed, no local driver | — | out of scope |

### Escape sequences: why generic ODBC works

Tableau, Excel, Qlik and Alteryx read the driver's `SQLGetInfo` capability bitmaps and then emit ODBC escape sequences — `{fn UCASE(x)}`, `{ts '...'}`, `{oj ...}`. The driver translates them into each backend's grammar:

- **Translated**: `{fn ...}` (scalar functions), `{d ...}` / `{t ...}` / `{ts ...}` (date/time/timestamp literals), `{escape ...}` (LIKE escape), `{oj ...}` (outer joins), `{interval ...}`.
- **Rejected with `HYC00`**: `{call ...}` — Argus exposes no procedures, consistent with `SQLProcedures` returning an empty set.
- **Rejected with `42000`** (naming the function): an escape the backend's dialect cannot render. It is never forwarded — `SQLGetInfo` never advertised it, and a clear driver error beats an opaque server syntax error.

The scalar-function bitmaps in `SQLGetInfo` (`SQL_STRING_FUNCTIONS`, `SQL_NUMERIC_FUNCTIONS`, `SQL_TIMEDATE_FUNCTIONS`, `SQL_SYSTEM_FUNCTIONS`) are **derived from the same per-backend dialect table** that drives the translator, so the driver cannot advertise a function it has no rendering for. Read the driver's answer via `SQLGetInfo` rather than trusting a table in a document.

The same dialect table drives `SQL_IDENTIFIER_QUOTE_CHAR`: ANSI double-quote for Trino/Phoenix/Pinot/Druid, backtick for Hive/Impala/MySQL-wire/BigQuery.

The function set differs per backend: Trino, Pinot, MySQL-wire and BigQuery dialects are verified against live servers; Hive/Impala are written from each engine's documented functions; Phoenix, Druid, Flight SQL and Kudu deliberately advertise a minimal set (`UCASE`, `LCASE`, `ABS`) until verified. If a server rejects a `{fn ...}` the driver advertised, that is a driver bug — please report it.

:::note ClickHouse
`BACKEND=mysql` deliberately omits `LOCATE`, `SPACE` and `DAYOFWEEK`: MariaDB/StarRocks/Doris support them, but ClickHouse (also reached with `BACKEND=mysql`) spells or numbers them differently. The driver refuses those three rather than send a query that would mean something else on ClickHouse.
:::

### Power BI

Power BI's generic **ODBC** source already works with Argus in Import mode: filters and GROUP BY fold to SQL. But no generic ODBC source can fold `LIMIT`/`TOP` — a Power Query architecture limit. The **Argus custom connector** declares, via `SqlCapabilities.LimitClauseKind`, how to emit top-N for each backend's dialect, which unlocks top-N folding and **DirectQuery**. (Snowflake, Databricks and Dremio ship the same driver-plus-connector pair.)

#### Install

1. Install the Argus ODBC driver (64-bit, matching 64-bit Power BI Desktop).
2. Download `Argus.mez` (or the signed `Argus.pqx`) from the [releases](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/argus/releases) and copy it to `Documents\Power BI Desktop\Custom Connectors\`. Restart Power BI Desktop.
3. Either:
   - **Unsigned `.mez`** — Options → Security → Data Extensions → *"(Not Recommended) Allow any extension to load..."*, or
   - **Signed `.pqx`** (preferred) — trust its certificate thumbprint via the `TrustedCertificateThumbprints` registry/GPO setting under `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Power BI Desktop`; no security downgrade required.

#### Use

**Get Data → Argus**, then supply Server, Port, Backend (`hive`, `impala`, `trino`, `phoenix`, `pinot`, `druid`, `mysql`, `bigquery`, `flightsql`; StarRocks/Doris/ClickHouse via `mysql`, Spark/Flink via `hive`) and optionally a database/catalog. Pick the authentication kind (Anonymous, Username/Password, or Windows for Kerberos via SSPI).

Apply a filter and a "Keep Top N" in Power Query — both **fold** (check *View Native Query*) — and you can switch the model to **DirectQuery**.

#### The ADBC transition does not affect Argus

Power BI and Fabric are [moving away from embedded ODBC drivers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/transition-to-adbc) toward ADBC (service end of 2026, Desktop spring 2027). Microsoft states this "doesn't change behavior for the ODBC connector when you use a separately installed ODBC driver" — which is what Argus is. Notably, Power BI's built-in **Hive** connector is deprecated with no replacement driver; Argus's `BACKEND=hive` serves HiveServer2 (and Spark and Flink) through a connector Microsoft is not retiring. See also the [Argus ADBC driver](./adbc.md).

### Tableau

Use the `.taco` where one exists — each connector fixes one SQL dialect:

| Connector | `BACKEND=` | Default port | Base dialect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `argus-trino` | `trino` | 8080 | `PrestoDialect` |
| `argus-hive` | `hive` (also Spark, Flink) | 10000 | `Hive12Dialect` |
| `argus-impala` | `impala` | 21050 | `Impala23Dialect` |
| `argus-mysql` | `mysql` (StarRocks/Doris — **not** ClickHouse) | 9030 | `MySQL8Dialect` |
| `argus-bigquery` | `bigquery` | — (REST) | `BigQuerySQLDialect` |

Install: copy the `.taco` to `Documents\My Tableau Repository\Connectors` — the driver itself must be installed separately. A `.taco` must be **signed with a public-CA code-signing certificate and timestamped** to load normally; unsigned connectors load only with verification disabled (`-DDisableVerifyConnectorPluginSignature=true` — development only).

**Verified with TDVT.** `argus-trino` has been run through Tableau's own
[Datasource Verification Tool](https://tableau.github.io/connector-plugin-sdk/docs/tdvt)
against a live Trino server — **91.4 %** of the expression suite (703/769), with
four native-Trino `dialect.tdd` overrides (`ROUND`, `ATAN2`, `ASCII`, `SPACE`).
At that point there are no Trino SQL errors and no driver bugs left; the
remaining differences are canonical TestV1 data conventions and PrestoDialect
empty-string edge cases. The turnkey harness (data loader, TDS files, run guide)
ships in `connectors/tableau/tdvt/`. See [How Argus compares](./comparison.md).

- **ClickHouse** is reached with `BACKEND=mysql` but is not covered by `argus-mysql` (its SQL is not MySQL's) — use generic ODBC for it.
- Backends with no `.taco` (phoenix, pinot, druid, flightsql) work through Tableau's generic **Other Databases (ODBC)** — functional, but Tableau [does not guarantee feature compatibility](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/examples_otherdatabases.htm) with it, and every machine opening the workbook needs the same DSN. Only 64-bit drivers are supported (Tableau 2023.3+).
- **Tableau Cloud** cannot host an ODBC driver: a Cloud workbook reaches Argus only through **Tableau Bridge** running on a machine with the driver and DSN installed.

### Excel

Excel **cannot load Power Query custom connectors** (`.mez`/`.pqx` are Power BI Desktop and the on-premises data gateway only). Excel reaches Argus through generic ODBC:

1. Install the Argus ODBC driver.
2. Create a DSN (64-bit `odbcad32.exe` on Windows).
3. **Data → Get Data → From Other Sources → From ODBC**, and pick the DSN.

Excel emits `{fn ...}`, so this depends entirely on the driver's escape translation — which is exactly what it is there for.

### Qlik

Qlik Sense on Windows and QlikView reach Argus through the built-in **Qlik ODBC Connector Package** — create a DSN and select it in the Data load editor. No Qlik-specific artifact is needed. **Qlik Sense SaaS** has no ODBC path.

### Alteryx, MicroStrategy, SSIS, SAS

Generic ODBC against a DSN. Nothing Argus-specific to install beyond the driver.

### DBeaver, Superset, Metabase, Looker

Out of reach for an ODBC driver: DBeaver is JDBC-only; Superset needs a SQLAlchemy dialect; Metabase needs a JDBC plugin; Looker/Looker Studio/QuickSight are managed services with no local driver hook. Several Argus target engines (Trino, Hive, Impala, StarRocks, BigQuery) have first-party JDBC drivers these tools support directly.

---

## How Argus compares

Argus is measured against the commercial baseline — Simba/Magnitude's SimbaEngine
drivers (OEM'd as the Databricks/Spark, Impala, Hive, Athena and BigQuery ODBC
drivers) and Starburst's Trino driver — and against the generic **Other Databases
(ODBC)** entry that BI tools ship. Parity is judged on the **observable ODBC
contract** (what the driver advertises and can do), not on marketing.

### At a glance

| | **Argus** | Simba / Starburst (per engine) | Generic *Other Databases (ODBC)* |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engines per driver | **10 in one binary** | one driver per engine | any, but dialect-blind |
| Licensing | **open** (Varga Foundation) | proprietary, per-seat | bundled |
| ODBC level | 3.8, Level 1, SQL-92 Entry | 3.8, Level 1/2 | depends on driver |
| Exported ODBC entry points | **107** | 89 (SimbaEngine core) | n/a |
| Unicode (`W`) | full | full | varies |
| Async execution | **yes** (`SQL_AM_STATEMENT`) | yes | usually no |
| Auth | Kerberos (GSSAPI+SSPI), OAuth2 (M2M + device flow), JWT, LDAP, TLS | yes | varies |
| Connection pooling | yes | yes | driver-manager only |
| Tableau TDVT | **91.4 %** measured | certified (>90 %) | not applicable |
| Large-result decode | DOM-free JSON (~65 % faster), spooling, Arrow via ADBC | Arrow / Cloud Fetch | row-wise |
| Dialect correctness | per-backend dialect + ODBC escape translation | per-engine | **none** — SQL passed through |
| Arrow surface | ADBC driver + Flight SQL backend | JDBC/ODBC | no |

### Why Argus

- **One driver, ten engines.** Commercial connectivity means a separate licensed
  driver per engine — Simba Spark *and* Simba Impala *and* Starburst Trino, each
  with its own installer, DSN scheme and support contract. Argus is a single
  binary with one connection-string grammar and a per-backend dialect layer, so a
  BI deployment installs and governs **one** driver.

- **At parity on the contract that matters, open.** ODBC 3.8, full Unicode, Level 1
  conformance, real asynchronous execution, connection pooling, the full auth
  matrix, a **broader raw ODBC surface (107 vs 89 entry points)**, and a
  **91.4 % Tableau TDVT** pass rate on the same tests certified connectors run —
  with no per-seat licence.

- **Honest capabilities.** Argus advertises only what it can do. Where an engine
  has no foreign keys, stored procedures or row-version columns, the catalog
  functions return empty — exactly as Simba's drivers for those engines do —
  rather than inventing metadata a BI tool would then trust.

- **Fast where it counts.** The Trino fetch path decodes result pages **without
  building a JSON DOM** — proven byte-identical to the reference path and ~65 %
  faster on large extracts (300 k × 9 columns: 573 ms vs 948 ms; 523 k vs 316 k
  rows/s) — on top of Trino spooling and a numeric fast-path that avoids a text
  round-trip.

- **Dialect-correct, unlike the generic ODBC entry.** Tableau itself
  [warns](https://help.tableau.com/current/pro/desktop/en-us/examples_otherdatabases.htm)
  that with *Other Databases (ODBC)* "the outcome may vary and compatibility …
  is not guaranteed". Argus ships a per-backend SQL dialect and translates ODBC
  escape sequences (`{fn …}`, `{d}`, `{t}`, `{ts}`, `{oj}`) into each engine's own
  grammar, so `{fn}`-generating tools (Tableau, Excel, Qlik) get correct SQL.

- **Sovereign and configurable.** Every Google endpoint is configurable for
  BigQuery, including S3NS sovereign clouds — connectivity that closed vendor
  drivers do not expose.

- **Arrow-native.** The same backends are exposed through an [Arrow ADBC
  driver](./adbc.md), and Arrow Flight SQL is a first-class backend.

### How this was measured

The comparison is evidence-based, not asserted:

- **Black-box ABI inspection** of real SimbaEngine binaries (the Spark and Hive
  ODBC drivers shipped with Power BI Desktop) — their exported ODBC entry points
  via `objdump`. The Simba Hive and Spark drivers export an *identical* 89-function
  surface, confirming the shared SimbaEngine core; Argus exports 107.
- **A live Tableau TDVT run** of the Argus Trino connector (769 expression tests)
  against a real Trino server.
- **A source audit** of the driver across the axes above.

No decompilation of proprietary binaries is involved — only their public ABI,
published documentation, and Argus's own source. The full write-up lives in the
repository at `docs/SIMBA_PARITY.md`.

:::note
"Parity" here is the ODBC contract a BI tool exercises. Simba retains an edge on
one thing worth a roadmap item: a native columnar **Arrow wire format** (Cloud
Fetch). Argus's DOM-free decode removes the dominant cost today, and the same
Arrow surface is already available through its ADBC driver.
:::

---

## Compatibility

### Tested versions

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| ODBC | 3.x API Level 1 (+ ODBC 2.x compatibility entry points) |
| unixODBC | 2.3.x |
| GLib | 2.56+ |
| CMake | 3.16+ |

### Supported backends

| Backend | `BACKEND=` | Protocol | Default Port | Notes |
|---------|-----------|----------|-------------|-------|
| Apache Hive | `hive` | Thrift TCLIService (V10), binary or HTTP | 10000 | HiveServer2 2.x, 3.x. Also serves **Spark Thrift Server**, **Flink SQL Gateway** and **Databricks** SQL warehouses (HiveServer2 protocol) |
| Apache Impala | `impala` | Thrift TCLIService (V6) | 21050 | Impala 3.x, 4.x |
| Trino | `trino` | HTTP REST API (JSON) | 8080 | Trino 400+ (v1), Trino 466+ (v2 spooling) |
| Apache Phoenix | `phoenix` | Avatica HTTP/JSON (PQS) | 8765 | Phoenix 5.x, PQS 6.x |
| Apache Pinot | `pinot` | HTTP/JSON (`/query/sql`) | 8000 (broker) | Validated end-to-end against a Pinot QuickStart cluster; table listing uses the controller (`:9000`) |
| Apache Druid | `druid` | HTTP/JSON (`/druid/v2/sql`) | 8888 (router) | Built on the validated Pinot/Trino HTTP-JSON pattern; broker is 8082 |
| Google BigQuery | `bigquery` | REST (`bigquery/v2`) | — | Public GCP, the BigQuery emulator, and sovereign clouds (e.g. S3NS) — every Google endpoint is configurable |
| MySQL-wire | `mysql` | MySQL client/server protocol | 3306 | **StarRocks** / **Apache Doris** (FE port 9030), **ClickHouse** (MySQL interface, port 9004), MySQL/MariaDB. Validated against MariaDB 11 |
| Arrow Flight SQL | `flightsql` | gRPC / Arrow Flight SQL | 32010 | **Dremio**, **InfluxDB 3** (port 8181), any Flight SQL server. Validated end-to-end against InfluxDB 3 Core |
| Apache Kudu | `kudu` | C++ Client API | 7051 | Kudu 1.15+. **Deprecated** — prefer `BACKEND=impala` (Impala queries Kudu tables natively) |

### Platforms

| Platform | Compiler | Status |
|----------|----------|--------|
| Linux (Ubuntu/Debian) | GCC | Supported (`.deb` packages, unixODBC) |
| Linux (Fedora/RHEL) | GCC | Supported |
| macOS | Clang | Supported |
| Windows (MSYS2/UCRT64) | MinGW | Supported — the installer ships Hive, Impala, Trino, Phoenix, Pinot, Druid, BigQuery and MySQL-wire; Flight SQL and Kudu need dependencies MSYS2 does not provide |

### ODBC entry points (103)

The driver exports 69 ANSI entry points plus 34 Unicode (`W`) variants — a
broader surface than the SimbaEngine core (89). See [How Argus compares](./comparison.md).

#### Environment & Handle
- SQLAllocHandle, SQLFreeHandle
- ODBC 2.x: SQLAllocEnv, SQLAllocConnect, SQLAllocStmt, SQLFreeEnv, SQLFreeConnect

#### Connection
- SQLConnect, SQLDriverConnect, SQLBrowseConnect, SQLDisconnect
- SQLGetConnectAttr, SQLSetConnectAttr

#### Statement
- SQLExecDirect, SQLExecute, SQLPrepare, SQLCancel, SQLNativeSql
- **Asynchronous execution**: `SQL_ATTR_ASYNC_ENABLE` (`SQL_AM_STATEMENT`), SQLCompleteAsync, SQLCancelHandle (ODBC 3.8)
- SQLBindParameter, SQLNumParams, SQLDescribeParam, SQLParamData, SQLPutData
- SQLNumResultCols, SQLDescribeCol, SQLColAttribute (and ODBC 2.x SQLColAttributes)
- SQLFetch, **SQLFetchScroll**, SQLExtendedFetch, SQLGetData, SQLBindCol
- SQLSetPos, SQLBulkOperations, SQLSetScrollOptions
- SQLCloseCursor, SQLFreeStmt, SQLGetCursorName, SQLSetCursorName
- SQLSetStmtAttr, SQLGetStmtAttr, SQLRowCount, SQLMoreResults

#### Catalog
- SQLTables, SQLColumns, SQLGetTypeInfo, SQLStatistics
- SQLPrimaryKeys, SQLForeignKeys, SQLProcedures, SQLProcedureColumns
- SQLSpecialColumns, SQLTablePrivileges, SQLColumnPrivileges

#### Descriptors
- SQLGetDescField, SQLSetDescField, SQLGetDescRec, SQLSetDescRec, SQLCopyDesc
- Unicode: SQLGetDescFieldW, SQLSetDescFieldW, SQLGetDescRecW

#### Info & Diagnostics
- SQLGetInfo, SQLGetDiagRec, SQLGetDiagField, SQLGetFunctions
- SQLSetEnvAttr, SQLGetEnvAttr, SQLEndTran (and ODBC 2.x SQLError, SQLTransact)

#### Cursors and block fetch

- **Block fetch**: `SQL_ATTR_ROW_ARRAY_SIZE` rowsets and `SQL_ATTR_PARAMSET_SIZE` parameter arrays.
- **Static scrollable cursors**: `SQLFetchScroll` with NEXT/PRIOR/FIRST/LAST/ABSOLUTE/RELATIVE.

#### Fetch performance

The Trino backend scans each result page **straight into cells without building
a JSON DOM** (the DOM was ~half of fetch time) — proven byte-identical to the
reference path and ~65 % faster end to end on large extracts. A kill-switch,
`ARGUS_TRINO_NOFASTJSON`, restores the DOM path. Numeric columns are kept as
native typed values so `SQLGetData` converts with no text round-trip, and Trino
v2 spooling is used where the server provides it.

### SQL dialects and identifier quoting

`SQLGetInfo(SQL_IDENTIFIER_QUOTE_CHAR)` is **dialect-aware** (since v0.5.9): ANSI double-quote (`"`) for Trino, Phoenix, Pinot and Druid; backtick (`` ` ``) for Hive, Impala, MySQL-wire and BigQuery. Tools that generate quoted SQL from this value (Power BI query folding, Tableau) get the right character per backend.

ODBC escape sequences (`{fn ...}`, `{d/t/ts ...}`, `{escape ...}`, `{oj ...}`, `{interval ...}`) are translated by the driver into each backend's grammar, and the scalar-function bitmaps reported by `SQLGetInfo` are derived from the same per-backend dialect table — the driver never advertises a function it cannot render. See [BI tools](./bi-tools.md).

### Type mapping

| Hive/Impala Type | Trino Type | Phoenix Type | Kudu Type | ODBC SQL Type |
|------------------|------------|--------------|-----------|---------------|
| BOOLEAN | boolean | BOOLEAN | BOOL | SQL_BIT |
| TINYINT | tinyint | TINYINT | INT8 | SQL_TINYINT |
| SMALLINT | smallint | SMALLINT | INT16 | SQL_SMALLINT |
| INT | integer | INTEGER | INT32 | SQL_INTEGER |
| BIGINT | bigint | BIGINT | INT64 | SQL_BIGINT |
| FLOAT | real | FLOAT | FLOAT | SQL_FLOAT / SQL_REAL |
| DOUBLE | double | DOUBLE | DOUBLE | SQL_DOUBLE |
| STRING / VARCHAR | varchar | VARCHAR | STRING / VARCHAR | SQL_VARCHAR |
| TIMESTAMP | timestamp | TIMESTAMP | UNIXTIME_MICROS | SQL_TYPE_TIMESTAMP |
| DATE | date | DATE | DATE | SQL_TYPE_DATE |
| DECIMAL | decimal | DECIMAL | DECIMAL | SQL_DECIMAL |
| BINARY | varbinary | VARBINARY / BINARY | BINARY | SQL_BINARY / SQL_VARBINARY |
| ARRAY / MAP / STRUCT | array / map / row | ARRAY | - | SQL_VARCHAR (JSON) |

Complex types (ARRAY, MAP, STRUCT) are serialized as JSON strings.

The HTTP/JSON backends (Pinot, Druid, BigQuery) and MySQL-wire map their native types onto the same ODBC SQL type set. The Flight SQL backend keeps numeric columns as **native typed values** (no per-cell string), so `SQLGetData` converts straight to the requested C type.

Timestamp values are accepted both as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS[.fff]` and as ISO-8601 with a `T` separator (as emitted by Druid).

#### Phoenix-specific types

Phoenix also supports unsigned variants (`UNSIGNED_TINYINT`, `UNSIGNED_SMALLINT`, `UNSIGNED_INT`, `UNSIGNED_LONG`, `UNSIGNED_FLOAT`, `UNSIGNED_DOUBLE`, `UNSIGNED_DATE`, `UNSIGNED_TIME`, `UNSIGNED_TIMESTAMP`) which map to their signed ODBC equivalents.

#### Kudu-specific types

Kudu uses `UNIXTIME_MICROS` for timestamps (microsecond precision since epoch). The Kudu backend converts these to standard `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff` format.

---

## Configuration

### Registering with unixODBC

#### Automatic

```bash
sudo bash scripts/install_dsn.sh
```

(The `.deb` package registers the driver for you.)

#### Manual

Add to `/etc/odbcinst.ini`:

```ini
[Argus]
Description = Argus ODBC Driver
Driver = /usr/local/lib/libargus_odbc.so
Setup = /usr/local/lib/libargus_odbc.so
```

Add a DSN to `/etc/odbc.ini` or `~/.odbc.ini`:

```ini
[ArgusHive]
Description = Hive via Argus
Driver = Argus
HOST = localhost
PORT = 10000
UID = hive
PWD =
DATABASE = default
AUTHMECH = NOSASL
BACKEND = hive
```

### Registering on Windows

The NSIS installer registers `Argus ODBC Driver` under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBCINST.INI` and bundles its DLLs. The driver reads DSNs from the registry: `HKCU\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBC.INI\<dsn>` first (user DSNs), then `HKLM` (system DSNs).

The driver setup has no configuration dialog, so create DSNs from PowerShell:

```powershell
Add-OdbcDsn -Name MyTrino -DriverName "Argus ODBC Driver" -DsnType User -Platform 64-bit `
    -SetPropertyValue @("BACKEND=trino", "HOST=trino.example.com", "PORT=8443", "SSL=1")

Remove-OdbcDsn -Name MyTrino -DsnType User -Platform 64-bit
```

:::caution
The Windows ODBC Manager rejects `UID`/`PWD` in a DSN's `-SetPropertyValue`. Supply credentials at connect time (the application's user/password fields) or in a DSN-less connection string instead.
:::

DSN-less connection strings (`DRIVER={Argus ODBC Driver};...`) need no DSN at all.

### Connection string parameters

| Parameter | Aliases | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|---------|-------------|
| HOST | SERVER | localhost | Server hostname or IP |
| PORT | | Per backend | Server port |
| UID | USERNAME, USER | (empty) | Username |
| PWD | PASSWORD | (empty) | Password (or token, for `JWT`/`BEARER`/`DATABRICKS`) |
| DATABASE | SCHEMA | default | Initial database/catalog |
| BACKEND | DRIVER_TYPE | hive | `hive`, `impala`, `trino`, `phoenix`, `pinot`, `druid`, `bigquery`, `mysql`, `flightsql`, `kudu` |
| AUTHMECH | AUTH | NOSASL | Authentication mechanism (see below) |
| KRBSERVICENAME | SERVICEPRINCIPALNAME | hive/impala | Kerberos SPN service name |
| KRBHOSTFQDN | KRBHOST | (HOST) | Kerberos SPN host, if it differs from HOST |
| KRBREALM | REALM | (from krb5.conf) | Explicit Kerberos realm |
| TransportMode | | BINARY | Hive/Impala transport: `BINARY` or `HTTP` |
| HTTPPath | | - | HTTP transport path (e.g. Databricks `/sql/1.0/warehouses/<id>`) |
| OAuth2TokenEndpoint | TokenURI | - | OAuth2 token endpoint (Trino) |
| OAuth2AuthEndpoint | AuthURI | - | OAuth2 authorization endpoint (`AUTH_CODE`) |
| OAuth2DeviceEndpoint | DeviceAuthURI | - | OAuth2 device-authorization endpoint (`DEVICE_CODE`) |
| OAuth2Issuer | Issuer | - | OIDC issuer — endpoints discovered via `/.well-known/openid-configuration` |
| ClientId / ClientSecret / Scope | | - | OAuth2 client parameters |
| SSL | UseSSL | false | Enable SSL/TLS |
| SSLCertFile | | - | Client certificate path (mutual TLS) |
| SSLKeyFile | | - | Client key path |
| SSLCAFile | | - | CA certificate path |
| SSLVerify | | true | Verify server certificate |
| LogLevel | | 0 | Log level (0=OFF to 6=TRACE) |
| LogFile | | stderr | Log file path |
| ConnectTimeout | | 0 | Connection timeout in seconds |
| QueryTimeout | | 0 | Query timeout in seconds |
| SocketTimeout | | 0 | Socket timeout in seconds |
| RetryCount | | 0 | Retry attempts on connect failure |
| RetryDelay | | 2 | Delay between retries in seconds |
| ApplicationName | AppName | - | Application identifier for query tracking |
| FetchBufferSize | | 1000 | Rows per fetch batch |
| TrinoProtocol | TRINO_PROTOCOL | v1 | Trino protocol version: `v1` (classic) or `v2` (spooling) |

BigQuery has its own parameter set (`Project`, `BQEndpoint`, `BQKeyFile`, ...) — see [Google BigQuery](#google-bigquery-backendbigquery) below.

#### Default ports by backend

| Backend | Default Port | Note |
|---------|-------------|------|
| hive | 10000 | |
| impala | 21050 | |
| trino | 8080 | |
| phoenix | 8765 | |
| pinot | 8000 | broker; table listing uses the controller on `:9000` |
| druid | 8888 | router; the broker is 8082 |
| bigquery | — | REST service, no host/port |
| mysql | 3306 | **set PORT explicitly**: StarRocks/Doris FE `9030`, ClickHouse `9004` |
| flightsql | 32010 | Dremio; InfluxDB 3 is `8181` |
| kudu | 7051 | deprecated |

#### Authentication mechanisms

| `AUTHMECH` value | Backends | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| NOSASL | hive, impala | No authentication (development/testing) |
| PLAIN / LDAP | hive, impala, trino | Username/password (SASL PLAIN for Thrift; HTTP Basic for Trino, requires `SSL=1`) |
| KERBEROS / GSSAPI | hive, impala, trino | Kerberos — system GSSAPI on Linux/macOS, **native SSPI on Windows** (no MIT Kerberos install). Trino uses SPNEGO/Negotiate |
| JWT / BEARER / DATABRICKS / TOKEN | hive (HTTP), trino | Bearer token taken from `PWD` |
| OAUTH2 / CLIENT_CREDENTIALS | trino | Machine-to-machine OAuth2; token auto-refreshed on `401` |
| DEVICE_CODE / DEVICE | trino | OAuth2 device authorization grant (RFC 8628), for headless logins |
| AUTH_CODE / BROWSER / SSO | trino | OAuth2 authorization code + PKCE, browser + loopback redirect |

See [Security](./security.md) for the details of each flow.

### Backend-specific notes

#### Hive (BACKEND=hive)

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=hive;HOST=hive.example.com;PORT=10000;UID=hive;DATABASE=default;AUTHMECH=NOSASL
```

- Protocol: Thrift TCLIService (binary, protocol V10) or HTTP (`TransportMode=HTTP`)
- Database set via `use:database` config in OpenSession
- **Authentication**: `NOSASL` (default), `PLAIN`/`LDAP`, `KERBEROS`/`GSSAPI` (SPN defaults to `hive/<host>`; override with `KrbServiceName`, `KrbHostFQDN`, `KrbRealm`). Over HTTP transport, `KERBEROS` uses SPNEGO and `JWT`/`BEARER`/`DATABRICKS` send a token from `PWD`

##### Spark and Flink

Apache Spark (Thrift Server) and Apache Flink (SQL Gateway `hiveserver2` endpoint) speak the HiveServer2 protocol — use `BACKEND=hive`:

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=hive;HOST=spark-thrift;PORT=10000;UID=spark;AuthMech=NOSASL
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=hive;HOST=flink-gateway;PORT=10000;UID=flink;AuthMech=NOSASL
```

(Spark Connect is a gRPC DataFrame API, not a SQL wire protocol — use the Thrift Server.)

##### Databricks

Databricks SQL warehouses speak HiveServer2 over HTTP with a bearer token (personal access token or OAuth token):

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=hive;HOST=<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com;PORT=443;SSL=1;TransportMode=HTTP;HTTPPath=/sql/1.0/warehouses/<id>;AuthMech=DATABRICKS;PWD={dapi...}
```

The same bearer-over-HTTP path covers any token-gated HiveServer2/Spark endpoint (e.g. behind Apache Knox with a JWT).

#### Impala (BACKEND=impala)

- Protocol: Thrift TCLIService (binary), protocol V6
- Database set via `USE <db>` statement after connect
- **Authentication**: same as Hive — `NOSASL`, `PLAIN`/`LDAP`, `KERBEROS`/`GSSAPI` (SPN defaults to `impala/<host>`)

#### Trino (BACKEND=trino)

- Protocol: HTTP REST API (JSON)
- DATABASE maps to Trino catalog via `X-Trino-Catalog` header
- Catalog operations via `information_schema` queries
- **v1 (default)**: Classic protocol — data is returned as flat JSON arrays in the response body
- **v2 (spooling)**: Requires Trino 466+. Data may be returned as spooled segments (inline base64 or external URIs). Enable with `TrinoProtocol=v2`. The driver automatically handles both inline and spooled segments, including fetching external data and acknowledging consumed segments
- **Authentication**: `LDAP`/`PLAIN` (HTTP Basic, requires `SSL=1`), `JWT`/`BEARER`, `KERBEROS` (SPNEGO), and the OAuth2 flows (`OAUTH2`, `DEVICE_CODE`, `AUTH_CODE`) with OIDC discovery via `OAuth2Issuer`

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=trino;HOST=trino;PORT=8443;SSL=1;AuthMech=OAUTH2;OAuth2TokenEndpoint=https://idp/token;ClientId=cid;ClientSecret=csec;Scope=trino
```

#### Phoenix (BACKEND=phoenix)

- Protocol: Avatica HTTP/JSON via Phoenix Query Server (PQS)
- DATABASE maps to the Phoenix/HBase schema
- Catalog operations via Avatica RPCs (`getTables`, `getColumns`, `getSchemas`, `getCatalogs`, `getTypeInfo`)
- Requires Phoenix Query Server running on the target host

#### Apache Pinot (BACKEND=pinot)

Real-time OLAP datastore. Argus queries the Pinot **broker**'s synchronous SQL endpoint (`POST /query/sql`) and lists tables from the **controller** (`/tables`, port 9000 on the same host).

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=pinot;HOST=pinot-broker;PORT=8000
```

- The whole result arrives in one response
- Optional HTTP Basic auth via `UID`/`PWD`; `SSL=1` for HTTPS
- Query errors surface the real Pinot message

#### Apache Druid (BACKEND=druid)

Real-time analytics database. Argus queries the broker/router's synchronous SQL endpoint (`POST /druid/v2/sql`, `resultFormat=array`) and uses Druid's `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` for catalog operations.

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=druid;HOST=druid-router;PORT=8888
```

- Optional HTTP Basic auth (`UID`/`PWD`); `SSL=1` for HTTPS
- Query errors surface the real Druid `errorMessage`

#### Google BigQuery (BACKEND=bigquery)

REST API (`bigquery/v2`). **Every Google URL is configurable**, so the driver works unchanged on sovereign-cloud deployments — e.g. S3NS, the trusted-cloud GCP offer operated by Thales — and against the BigQuery emulator.

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `Project` / `BQProject` | GCP project id (**required**) | - |
| `Database` / `Schema` | Default dataset | - |
| `BQLocation` | Job location (`EU`, `europe-west9`, ...) | - |
| `BQEndpoint` | API base URL | `https://bigquery.googleapis.com` |
| `BQTokenEndpoint` | OAuth2 token endpoint | `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` or the key file's `token_uri` |
| `BQAudience` | JWT `aud` claim | the token endpoint |
| `BQScope` | OAuth2 scope | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/bigquery` |
| `BQKeyFile` | Service-account JSON key path (RS256 JWT-bearer grant; needs OpenSSL) | - |
| `AccessToken` | Pre-fetched bearer token (skips the token flow) | - |

Public GCP with a service-account key:

```
Backend=bigquery;Project=my-project;Database=my_dataset;BQKeyFile=/etc/argus/sa-key.json;BQLocation=EU
```

Sovereign cloud (custom API + IAM endpoints, audience, private CA — `SSLCAFile` is honoured for **both** the API and the token endpoint):

```
Backend=bigquery;Project=my-project;
BQEndpoint=https://bigquery.s3ns.example;
BQTokenEndpoint=https://iam.s3ns.example/token;
BQAudience=https://iam.s3ns.example/token;
BQKeyFile=/etc/argus/sa-key.json;
SSL=1;SSLVerify=1;SSLCAFile=/etc/argus/s3ns-ca.pem
```

For mutual TLS, add `SSLCertFile=` / `SSLKeyFile=`. Emulator/tests (no auth): `Backend=bigquery;Project=test;BQEndpoint=http://localhost:9050`.

#### MySQL-wire (BACKEND=mysql)

A single backend serves every engine that speaks the MySQL client/server protocol, via libmariadb: **StarRocks**, **Apache Doris**, **ClickHouse** (MySQL interface), and MySQL/MariaDB themselves.

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=mysql;HOST=starrocks-fe;PORT=9030;UID=root;DATABASE=analytics
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=mysql;HOST=clickhouse;PORT=9004;UID=default;DATABASE=default
```

- A database is reported as an ODBC **catalog** (`TABLE_CAT`); the schema column is left empty, following the MySQL Connector/ODBC convention
- Catalog operations run against `information_schema`
- `SSL=1` enables TLS (`SSLCertFile`/`SSLKeyFile`/`SSLCAFile`, `SSLVerify` honored)

#### Arrow Flight SQL (BACKEND=flightsql)

Reaches any engine exposing an Arrow Flight SQL endpoint — **Dremio**, **InfluxDB 3** — over gRPC.

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=flightsql;HOST=dremio;PORT=32010;UID=user;PWD={secret}
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=flightsql;HOST=influxdb3;PORT=443;SSL=1;PWD={token}
```

- Record batches are **streamed** lazily (one block per fetch, bounded memory); numeric columns are kept as native typed values
- `DATABASE` is sent as the gRPC `database` call header (how InfluxDB 3 selects the target database)
- Auth: `UID`+`PWD` → Flight handshake (basic token); `PWD` alone → `Bearer` token (JWT)
- `SSL=1` uses a TLS gRPC channel

#### Apache Kudu (BACKEND=kudu) — deprecated

:::caution Deprecated — use the Impala backend instead
Kudu is normally queried through Impala (which plans and executes SQL against Kudu tables natively), and `libkudu_client` is not packaged for any Ubuntu newer than 16.04. The `kudu` backend still builds where the client library is available, but is in maintenance mode.

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=impala;HOST=impalad;PORT=21050;DATABASE=default
```
:::

If used directly: HOST points to the Kudu master; only `SELECT` is supported through a minimal SQL parser (`SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... LIMIT`; operators `=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `!=`, `IN`, `IS [NOT] NULL`). `JOIN`, `GROUP BY`, `ORDER BY`, subqueries and DML are not supported.

### Parameter priority

When the same parameter is specified multiple ways:

1. Connection string (highest)
2. DSN configuration
3. Environment variable
4. Default value (lowest)

### Environment variables

```bash
export ARGUS_LOG_LEVEL=5    # Log level
export ARGUS_LOG_FILE=/tmp/argus.log  # Log file
```

```c
SQLConnect(dbc, "ArgusHive", SQL_NTS, "hive", SQL_NTS, "", SQL_NTS);
```

### DSN-less connections (SQLDriverConnect)

#### Hive

```
HOST=hive-server;PORT=10000;UID=admin;PWD=secret;DATABASE=mydb;BACKEND=hive
```

#### Impala

```
HOST=impala-server;PORT=21050;UID=admin;PWD=secret;DATABASE=mydb;BACKEND=impala
```

#### Trino

```
HOST=trino-server;PORT=8080;UID=admin;DATABASE=hive;BACKEND=trino
```

#### Phoenix

```
HOST=phoenix-server;PORT=8765;UID=admin;DATABASE=myschema;BACKEND=phoenix
```

#### Pinot

```
HOST=pinot-broker;PORT=8000;BACKEND=pinot
```

#### Druid

```
HOST=druid-router;PORT=8888;BACKEND=druid
```

#### BigQuery

```
BACKEND=bigquery;Project=my-project;Database=my_dataset;BQKeyFile=/etc/argus/sa-key.json;BQLocation=EU
```

#### StarRocks / Doris / ClickHouse (MySQL-wire)

```
HOST=starrocks-fe;PORT=9030;UID=root;DATABASE=analytics;BACKEND=mysql
HOST=doris-fe;PORT=9030;UID=admin;PWD=secret;DATABASE=ods;BACKEND=mysql
HOST=clickhouse;PORT=9004;UID=default;DATABASE=default;BACKEND=mysql
```

#### Dremio / InfluxDB 3 (Flight SQL)

```
HOST=dremio;PORT=32010;UID=user;PWD=secret;BACKEND=flightsql
HOST=influxdb3;PORT=443;SSL=1;PWD=token;DATABASE=mydb;BACKEND=flightsql
```

#### Spark Thrift Server / Flink SQL Gateway (via the Hive backend)

```
HOST=spark-thrift;PORT=10000;UID=spark;AUTHMECH=NOSASL;BACKEND=hive
HOST=flink-gateway;PORT=10000;UID=flink;AUTHMECH=NOSASL;BACKEND=hive
```

### Authentication examples

#### Hive with Kerberos

Linux/macOS use the system GSSAPI (`kinit` ticket or keytab); Windows uses the logged-in domain user via SSPI.

```
HOST=hive.example.com;PORT=10000;BACKEND=hive;
AUTHMECH=KERBEROS;KrbServiceName=hive;
SSL=1;SSLCAFile=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
```

#### Databricks SQL warehouse (personal access token)

```
HOST=<workspace>.cloud.databricks.com;PORT=443;SSL=1;BACKEND=hive;
TransportMode=HTTP;HTTPPath=/sql/1.0/warehouses/<id>;
AUTHMECH=DATABRICKS;PWD=dapi...
```

#### Trino with LDAP (HTTP Basic over TLS)

```
HOST=trino.example.com;PORT=8443;SSL=1;BACKEND=trino;
UID=analyst;PWD=secret;AUTHMECH=LDAP
```

#### Trino with OAuth2 client credentials

```
HOST=trino.example.com;PORT=8443;SSL=1;BACKEND=trino;
AUTHMECH=OAUTH2;OAuth2Issuer=https://idp.example.com;
ClientId=svc-trino;ClientSecret=***;Scope=trino
```

#### Trino with browser SSO (authorization code + PKCE)

```
HOST=trino.example.com;PORT=8443;SSL=1;BACKEND=trino;
AUTHMECH=SSO;OAuth2Issuer=https://idp.example.com;ClientId=trino-desktop
```

### Production configurations

#### Hive with SSL and logging

```
HOST=hive.example.com;PORT=10000;UID=admin;PWD=secret;
SSL=1;SSLCAFile=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt;SSLVerify=1;
LogLevel=4;LogFile=/var/log/argus-hive.log;
BACKEND=hive;ApplicationName=ETL-Pipeline
```

#### Impala with retry and timeout

```
HOST=impala.example.com;PORT=21050;UID=admin;PWD=secret;
DATABASE=warehouse;BACKEND=impala;
RetryCount=3;RetryDelay=2;
ConnectTimeout=30;QueryTimeout=600;SocketTimeout=120;
FetchBufferSize=5000;ApplicationName=Analytics
```

#### Trino with HTTPS and mutual TLS

```
HOST=trino.example.com;PORT=8443;UID=admin;PWD=secret;
SSL=1;SSLVerify=1;
SSLCertFile=/etc/ssl/certs/client-cert.pem;
SSLKeyFile=/etc/ssl/private/client-key.pem;
SSLCAFile=/etc/ssl/certs/trino-ca.pem;
BACKEND=trino;LogLevel=5;ApplicationName=Dashboard
```

#### Trino with v2 spooling protocol

```
HOST=trino.example.com;PORT=8443;UID=admin;
SSL=1;SSLVerify=1;SSLCAFile=/etc/ssl/certs/trino-ca.pem;
BACKEND=trino;TrinoProtocol=v2;ApplicationName=DataPipeline
```

#### BigQuery on a sovereign cloud (S3NS-style)

```
BACKEND=bigquery;Project=my-project;
BQEndpoint=https://bigquery.s3ns.example;
BQTokenEndpoint=https://iam.s3ns.example/token;
BQAudience=https://iam.s3ns.example/token;
BQKeyFile=/etc/argus/sa-key.json;
SSL=1;SSLVerify=1;SSLCAFile=/etc/argus/s3ns-ca.pem
```

#### Phoenix with timeout

```
HOST=pqs.example.com;PORT=8765;UID=admin;
DATABASE=myschema;BACKEND=phoenix;
ConnectTimeout=30;QueryTimeout=300;
LogLevel=4;LogFile=/var/log/argus-phoenix.log;
ApplicationName=HBase-Analytics
```

### C/C++ usage

#### Connect and query

```c
SQLHENV env;
SQLHDBC dbc;
SQLHSTMT stmt;

SQLAllocHandle(SQL_HANDLE_ENV, SQL_NULL_HANDLE, &env);
SQLSetEnvAttr(env, SQL_ATTR_ODBC_VERSION, (void*)SQL_OV_ODBC3, 0);
SQLAllocHandle(SQL_HANDLE_DBC, env, &dbc);

const char *conn_str =
    "HOST=hive-server;PORT=10000;UID=admin;PWD=secret;"
    "DATABASE=mydb;BACKEND=hive;LogLevel=5";

SQLDriverConnect(dbc, NULL, (SQLCHAR*)conn_str, SQL_NTS,
                 NULL, 0, NULL, SQL_DRIVER_NOPROMPT);

SQLAllocHandle(SQL_HANDLE_STMT, dbc, &stmt);
SQLExecDirect(stmt, (SQLCHAR*)"SELECT * FROM my_table", SQL_NTS);

SQLCHAR col1[256];
SQLLEN ind;
SQLBindCol(stmt, 1, SQL_C_CHAR, col1, sizeof(col1), &ind);

while (SQLFetch(stmt) == SQL_SUCCESS) {
    printf("%s\n", col1);
}

SQLFreeHandle(SQL_HANDLE_STMT, stmt);
SQLDisconnect(dbc);
SQLFreeHandle(SQL_HANDLE_DBC, dbc);
SQLFreeHandle(SQL_HANDLE_ENV, env);
```

#### Block fetch (rowsets)

```c
#define ROWS 100
SQLCHAR names[ROWS][64];
SQLLEN inds[ROWS];
SQLULEN fetched = 0;

SQLSetStmtAttr(stmt, SQL_ATTR_ROW_ARRAY_SIZE, (SQLPOINTER)ROWS, 0);
SQLSetStmtAttr(stmt, SQL_ATTR_ROWS_FETCHED_PTR, &fetched, 0);
SQLBindCol(stmt, 1, SQL_C_CHAR, names, 64, inds);

while (SQLFetchScroll(stmt, SQL_FETCH_NEXT, 0) == SQL_SUCCESS) {
    for (SQLULEN i = 0; i < fetched; i++)
        printf("%s\n", names[i]);
}
```

#### Query cancellation

```c
/* Execute in background thread */
SQLExecDirect(stmt, (SQLCHAR*)"SELECT * FROM huge_table", SQL_NTS);

/* Cancel from another thread */
SQLCancel(stmt);
```

```powershell
    -SetPropertyValue @("BACKEND=trino", "HOST=trino.example.com", "PORT=8443", "SSL=1")
```

(`UID`/`PWD` cannot be set in DSN properties on Windows — supply them at connect time.)

## FAQ

- **Which ODBC driver manager is supported?** unixODBC on Linux/macOS (driver v0.5.8+), Windows ODBC Driver Manager on Windows.
- **Can I use Argus with Power BI?** Yes. Generic ODBC works in Import mode, and the packaged **Argus custom connector** (`Argus.mez`/`.pqx`) additionally unlocks top-N query folding and DirectQuery. See [BI tools](./bi-tools.md#power-bi).
- **Can I use Argus with Tableau?** Yes. Packaged `.taco` connectors exist for Trino, Hive (also Spark/Flink), Impala, StarRocks/Doris and BigQuery; other backends work through Tableau's generic ODBC entry. See [BI tools](./bi-tools.md#tableau).
- **Can I use Argus with Excel / Qlik / Alteryx / SAS?** Yes, through generic ODBC with a DSN. The driver translates the ODBC escape sequences (`{fn ...}`, `{ts ...}`, `{oj ...}`) these tools emit, per backend dialect.
- **Does Argus support Kerberos?** Yes. Hive and Impala authenticate with `AuthMech=KERBEROS` — system GSSAPI on Linux/macOS (a `kinit` ticket or keytab), **native SSPI on Windows** (the logged-in domain user, no MIT Kerberos install). Trino uses SPNEGO/Negotiate. The Kudu backend uses Kerberos natively via its C++ client.
- **Does Argus support OAuth2 / SSO?** Yes, for Trino: client credentials, device code (RFC 8628), and authorization code with PKCE + browser SSO, with OIDC discovery (`OAuth2Issuer`). See [Security](./security.md#oauth2-trino).
- **Can I connect to Databricks?** Yes — Databricks SQL warehouses speak HiveServer2 over HTTP: `BACKEND=hive;TransportMode=HTTP;HTTPPath=/sql/1.0/warehouses/<id>;AuthMech=DATABRICKS` with the personal access token in `PWD`.
- **Can I connect to Spark or Flink?** Yes — Spark Thrift Server and Flink SQL Gateway speak the HiveServer2 protocol: use `BACKEND=hive`.
- **Can I connect to StarRocks, Doris or ClickHouse?** Yes — they speak the MySQL wire protocol: use `BACKEND=mysql` (StarRocks/Doris FE port `9030`, ClickHouse `9004`).
- **What is ADBC and does Argus support it?** Arrow ADBC is a columnar database API. Argus ships `libargus_adbc` over the same backends, returning results as Arrow C Data Interface streams. See [ADBC](./adbc.md). The Power BI/Fabric ADBC transition does not affect Argus's ODBC path (it only retires drivers Microsoft embeds).
- **Do I need all backends installed?** No. Dependencies are optional per backend and auto-detected at build time. Install only the libraries for backends you use.
- **How are complex types handled?** ARRAY, MAP, and STRUCT are serialized as JSON strings via SQL_VARCHAR.
- **Can I use Argus with connection pooling?** Yes. The driver is designed to be connection-pooling ready.
- **What is the default fetch batch size?** 1000 rows. Configurable via `FetchBufferSize`. Block fetch (`SQL_ATTR_ROW_ARRAY_SIZE` + `SQLFetchScroll`) and static scrollable cursors are supported.
- **Does Argus support prepared statements?** SQLPrepare is implemented and dispatches to the backend's execute function; `SQLBindParameter` binds `?` markers.
- **Does Argus support `{call ...}` (stored procedures)?** No — procedure escapes are rejected with `HYC00`, consistent with `SQLProcedures` returning an empty result set.
- **Why does Argus refuse a `{fn ...}` my tool generated?** The backend's dialect has no rendering for that function, so the driver rejects it with `42000` and the function's name instead of forwarding SQL that would fail (or silently mean something else) server-side. If the server actually supports the function, that is a dialect-table bug — please report it.
- **What is Phoenix Query Server?** Phoenix Query Server (PQS) is a standalone server that provides remote access to Apache Phoenix via the Avatica protocol over HTTP/JSON. The Argus Phoenix backend connects to PQS, not directly to HBase — and requires it.
- **What is the difference between Trino v1 and v2 protocol?** v1 (default) returns data as flat JSON arrays inline in the REST response. v2 (spooling, Trino 466+) can offload large result sets to external storage and return them as segments. Use `TrinoProtocol=v2` to enable spooling; the driver handles both formats transparently, including mixed responses.
- **When should I use Trino v2 spooling?** For large result sets on Trino 466+: spooling reduces coordinator memory pressure. For small queries or older Trino versions, v1 is sufficient.
- **Should I use the Kudu backend?** No — it is **deprecated**. Query Kudu tables through Impala (`BACKEND=impala`), which plans and executes SQL against Kudu natively. The direct backend remains read-only `SELECT` with a minimal SQL parser and only builds where `libkudu_client` is available.

---

## Introduction

Argus is a production-ready ODBC driver that provides SQL connectivity to multiple analytics query engines. It implements the ODBC 3.x API with a pluggable backend architecture supporting **ten backends** — Apache Hive, Apache Impala, Trino, Apache Phoenix, Apache Pinot, Apache Druid, Google BigQuery, MySQL-wire engines (StarRocks, Apache Doris, ClickHouse), Arrow Flight SQL (Dremio, InfluxDB 3) and Apache Kudu — plus an **Arrow ADBC driver** built over the same stack.

### Features

- **103 ODBC entry points** (69 ANSI + 34 Unicode `W` variants): ODBC 3.x API Level 1, plus ODBC 2.x compatibility (`SQLAllocConnect`, `SQLError`, `SQLExtendedFetch`, ...).
- **10 backends** through a single driver, enabled by dependency auto-detection at build time.
- **Statement-level asynchronous execution** (`SQL_ASYNC_MODE = SQL_AM_STATEMENT`, `SQLCompleteAsync`, `SQLCancelHandle`).
- **Arrow ADBC driver** (`libargus_adbc`) exposing the same backends through the Arrow C Data Interface — see [ADBC](./adbc.md).
- **BI tool support**: ODBC escape-sequence translation (`{fn ...}`, `{ts ...}`, `{oj ...}`) per backend dialect, plus a packaged [Power BI custom connector and Tableau connectors](./bi-tools.md) — verified with Tableau's TDVT (**91.4 %**). How Argus stacks up against Simba/Starburst: [How Argus compares](./comparison.md).
- **Authentication**: SASL PLAIN/LDAP, **Kerberos** (system GSSAPI on Linux/macOS, native SSPI on Windows), JWT/Bearer tokens (Databricks), and **OAuth2** for Trino — client credentials, device code (RFC 8628) and authorization code with PKCE + browser SSO, with OIDC discovery.
- **Cross-Platform**: Linux, macOS, and Windows x64.
- **SSL/TLS**: Secure connections with certificate verification (and mutual TLS) for all backends.
- **Connection Resilience**: Automatic retry, configurable timeouts, query cancellation.
- **Fetch performance**: configurable batching, block fetch (`SQL_ATTR_ROW_ARRAY_SIZE`), static scrollable cursors (`SQLFetchScroll`), and a **DOM-free Trino decode** (~65 % faster on large extracts).
- **Production Logging**: 7 log levels, thread-safe, file or stderr output.

### Architecture

Argus uses a two-layer pluggable architecture.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Application                     │
│      ODBC / ADBC application or BI tool          │
└────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                     │
┌────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐
│               ODBC API Layer                     │
│  Handle Mgmt ─► Connect ─► Execute ─► Fetch      │
│  Catalog ─► Dialects & escape translation        │
│  Diagnostics ─► Logging                          │
└────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                     │  backend vtable
┌────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐
│              Backend Abstraction                 │
│  Hive · Impala · Trino · Phoenix · Pinot ·       │
│  Druid · BigQuery · MySQL-wire · Flight SQL ·    │
│  Kudu (deprecated)                               │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Layer 1 — ODBC API** (`src/odbc/`): Implements the ODBC specification. Handles environment, connection, and statement lifecycle, connection string parsing, type conversion, diagnostics, and the **per-backend SQL dialect table** — identifier quote character and ODBC escape-sequence translation, from which the `SQLGetInfo` capability bitmaps are derived. Never talks to a database directly.

**Layer 2 — Backend Abstraction** (`src/backend/`): Each backend implements the `argus_backend_t` vtable covering connection lifecycle, query execution, result fetching, catalog operations, and cancellation.

| `BACKEND=` | Engine | Protocol | Default port |
|------------|--------|----------|-------------|
| `hive` | Apache Hive — also Spark Thrift Server and Flink SQL Gateway (HiveServer2 protocol) | Thrift binary or HTTP | 10000 |
| `impala` | Apache Impala | Thrift binary | 21050 |
| `trino` | Trino | HTTP REST (JSON) | 8080 |
| `phoenix` | Apache Phoenix (Avatica/PQS) | HTTP/JSON | 8765 |
| `pinot` | Apache Pinot | HTTP/JSON | 8000 |
| `druid` | Apache Druid | HTTP/JSON | 8888 |
| `bigquery` | Google BigQuery — incl. sovereign clouds (S3NS): every Google endpoint is configurable | REST/JSON | — |
| `mysql` | StarRocks / Doris / ClickHouse / MySQL / MariaDB | MySQL wire | 3306 |
| `flightsql` | Dremio / InfluxDB 3 / any Arrow Flight SQL server | gRPC / Arrow | 32010 |
| `kudu` | Apache Kudu (**deprecated** — prefer `BACKEND=impala`) | kudu_client | 7051 |

Enable standard ODBC-based applications to query distributed SQL systems without backend-specific code.
