```powershell
irm https://choregos.example.com/cli/install.ps1 | iex
```

The script picks the file for your system, checks its SHA-256 against the instance's manifest, and
puts `choregos` on your path.

**By hand**, download the file for your system from your instance:

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| Linux, x86-64 | `choregos-linux-x86_64` |
| Linux, ARM64 | `choregos-linux-arm64` |
| macOS, Apple silicon | `choregos-macos-arm64` |
| macOS, Intel | `choregos-macos-x86_64` |
| Windows, x86-64 | `choregos-windows-x86_64.exe` |

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://choregos.example.com/downloads/cli/choregos-linux-x86_64
curl -fsSL https://choregos.example.com/downloads/cli/manifest.json
```

`manifest.json` gives the version and, for each file, its system, architecture, size and `sha256`.
Compare it with the file you downloaded:

```shell
sha256sum choregos-linux-x86_64
chmod +x choregos-linux-x86_64 && mv choregos-linux-x86_64 ~/.local/bin/choregos
```

On macOS, `shasum -a 256` gives the same digest. The same files, a `SHA256SUMS` file and their
signatures are also attached to each
[GitHub release](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/releases), under the same names.

An instance built without the CLI says so on its Integrations page; ask your operator, or use the
GitHub release.

### Keep it at your instance's version

The CLI tells you when its version differs from your instance's. Replace it with the instance's own
build:

```shell
choregos self update
```

### From the GitHub release

This works on every version, and is the way on 0.25.3 and earlier. It needs Python 3.12 and
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Download three wheels of your instance's version from its
[GitHub release](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/releases) (here 0.26.1):
`choregos_cli-0.26.1-py3-none-any.whl`, `choregos_core-0.26.1-py3-none-any.whl` and
`choregos_contracts-0.26.1-py3-none-any.whl`. Then:

```shell
uv tool install --python 3.12 ./choregos_cli-0.26.1-py3-none-any.whl \
  --with ./choregos_core-0.26.1-py3-none-any.whl --with ./choregos_contracts-0.26.1-py3-none-any.whl
```

To upgrade, install the next version's
wheels the same way with `--force`.

### Sign in

The CLI cannot issue its first token: create a full-access token in the console, menu under your
name, **My account**, *Access tokens*, **Create an API token (90 days)**. Then:

```bash
choregos login --api-url https://choregos.example.com --token chg_... --org acme
choregos whoami
```

**What you should see:** `whoami` prints who you are and your roles. The profile is saved in
`~/.config/choregos/config.json` (`CHOREGOS_CONFIG` names another file). Without a profile, the CLI
reads `CHOREGOS_API_URL`, `CHOREGOS_TOKEN` and `CHOREGOS_ORG`, which suits a CI job.

### What can go wrong

| Symptom | Why | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cannot reach http://localhost:8000` | no profile yet | `choregos login --api-url …` |
| `401` | the token is unknown, revoked or expired | create a new one in **My account** |
| `403` on every command | an MCP or A2A token in the profile | the CLI needs a full-access (`*`) token |
| `no organisation` | neither `--org`, the profile nor `CHOREGOS_ORG` names one | `choregos login --org acme`, or `choregos orgs list` |
| the digest does not match | an incomplete or altered download | download again; do not run the file |

### Go further

- [CLI reference](reference.md): every command and option.
- [Start a workflow over A2A](../integrate/a2a.md) with `choregos a2a`.

---

## CLI reference

This page is generated from the CLI itself, and the repository's tests fail when it differs from the
commands. `choregos <command> --help` prints the same text for the version you installed
([Install the CLI](install.md)).

The profile lives in `~/.config/choregos/config.json` (`CHOREGOS_CONFIG` names another file):
`api_url`, `token`, `org`. `choregos login` writes it; `CHOREGOS_API_URL`, `CHOREGOS_TOKEN` and
`CHOREGOS_ORG` are read when no profile exists.

### `choregos a2a`

Start and follow a workflow over the A2A door (an `a2a` token)

#### `choregos a2a cancel`

```text
Usage: choregos a2a cancel [OPTIONS] {task}

  Stop a task: its work item is stopped, as from the console.

Arguments:
  task  the task id `send` printed  [required]

Options:
  --org <str>    the organisation; the profile's otherwise
  --token <str>  an `a2a` token; the profile's token otherwise, which the door
                 refuses when it is `*`  [env var: CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN]
  --json         print the task as the door answers it, for a script
  --help         Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos a2a follow`

```text
Usage: choregos a2a follow [OPTIONS] {task}

  Follow a task to its end, over the stream, opened again when the door cuts
  it (an hour at most).

  Exit 0 completed, 3 failed, 4 canceled. A decision is printed with its URL;
  the task waits for it.

Arguments:
  task  the task id `send` printed  [required]

Options:
  --out <path>   write the artefacts of a completed task in this directory
  --org <str>    the organisation; the profile's otherwise
  --token <str>  an `a2a` token; the profile's token otherwise, which the door
                 refuses when it is `*`  [env var: CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN]
  --json         print the task as the door answers it, for a script
  --help         Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos a2a get`

```text
Usage: choregos a2a get [OPTIONS] {task}

  Read a task once: its state, the decision it waits for, its artefacts.

Arguments:
  task  the task id `send` printed  [required]

Options:
  --out <path>   write the artefacts of a completed task in this directory
  --org <str>    the organisation; the profile's otherwise
  --token <str>  an `a2a` token; the profile's token otherwise, which the door
                 refuses when it is `*`  [env var: CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN]
  --json         print the task as the door answers it, for a script
  --help         Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos a2a send`

```text
Usage: choregos a2a send [OPTIONS] {skill}

  Start a workflow: a text, fields and files in one message. The message id is
  printed first.

Arguments:
  skill  the skill, `project/skill` as `choregos a2a skills` lists it
         [required]

Options:
  --text <str>          the request in words, the work item's body
                        (repeatable)
  --field <str>         `key=value` (repeatable), a value read as JSON when it
                        is JSON
  --fields-json <path>  a file holding the fields as one JSON object (`-` for
                        stdin)
  --file <str>          `PATH` or `PATH;type=MEDIA/TYPE`, sent in base64
                        (repeatable)
  --message-id <str>    the idempotency key; by default a digest of the
                        message, so the same command finds the same task
  --title <str>         the work item's title
  --wait                follow the task to its end: exit 0 completed, 3
                        failed, 4 canceled
  --out <path>          write the artefacts of a completed task in this
                        directory
  --org <str>           the organisation; the profile's otherwise
  --token <str>         an `a2a` token; the profile's token otherwise, which
                        the door refuses when it is `*`  [env var:
                        CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN]
  --json                print the task as the door answers it, for a script
  --help                Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos a2a skills`

```text
Usage: choregos a2a skills [OPTIONS]

  The workflows this token may start, and the fields each takes (`*` =
  required).

Options:
  --org <str>    the organisation; the profile's otherwise
  --token <str>  an `a2a` token; the profile's token otherwise, which the door
                 refuses when it is `*`  [env var: CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN]
  --json         print the task as the door answers it, for a script
  --help         Show this message and exit.
```

```text
  --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

### `choregos orgs`

Organisations

#### `choregos orgs create`

```text
Usage: choregos orgs create [OPTIONS] {slug}

  Create an organisation (requires being an admin of an organisation already).

Arguments:
  slug  [required]

Options:
  --name <str>
  --help        Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos orgs list`

```text
Usage: choregos orgs list [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

### `choregos plugin`

Plugins: validate, pack and index them (ADR 0093)

#### `choregos plugin index`

```text
Usage: choregos plugin index [OPTIONS] {directory}

  Write a source index (plugin-index.schema.json) for every plugin under
  DIRECTORY, located either in an OCI repository or in a git commit.

Arguments:
  directory  A directory whose subdirectories are plugins.  [required]

Options:
  -o, --output <path>     The index to write (index.yaml).  [required]
  --oci-repository <str>  Plugins are published as
                          <repository>/<name>:<version>.
  --git-url <str>         Plugins are read from this repository.
  --git-commit <str>      The commit (40 hex characters) they are read at.
  --git-path <str>        Where DIRECTORY sits in the repository, e.g.
                          plugins.
  --help                  Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos plugin pack`

```text
Usage: choregos plugin pack [OPTIONS] {directory}

  Validate, then write a reproducible archive of the declared files only
  (plugin.yaml, README.md and LICENSE when present, and what `contents`
  names): sorted entries, time 0, owner 0. The same files always give the same
  bytes, and the printed digest is the one an index records.

Arguments:
  directory  The plugin directory.  [required]

Options:
  -o, --output <path>  The archive to write (.tar.gz).  [required]
  --help               Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos plugin validate`

```text
Usage: choregos plugin validate [OPTIONS] {path}

  Check a plugin and everything it ships; print its name, version and content
  digest. Only what plugin.yaml declares is read: a server's source or a .venv
  beside it is ignored.

Arguments:
  path  A plugin directory or a packed .tar.gz.  [required]

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

### `choregos projects`

Projects

#### `choregos projects create`

```text
Usage: choregos projects create [OPTIONS] {slug}

  Create a project; `--template` then starts the provisioning.

  Without `--repo`, the project has no repository (ADR 0012): the agent works
  in an empty directory, and requests are filed with `choregos items create`.

Arguments:
  slug  [required]

Options:
  --repo <str>      URL of the application repository (optional: work without
                    code has none)
  --name <str>
  --template <str>
  --org <str>
  --language <str>  [default: python]
  --tracker <str>   `internal`: requests are filed in Choregos. Without
                    `--repo` the default is `internal`; with `--repo` it is
                    written only when given
  --help            Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos projects list`

```text
Usage: choregos projects list [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --org <str>
  --help       Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos projects provision`

```text
Usage: choregos projects provision [OPTIONS] {project}

  Start (or restart) the provisioning, and follow it live with `--follow`.

Arguments:
  project  [required]

Options:
  --follow
  --help    Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos projects readiness`

```text
  What the project still lacks to run, and who can fix each item. Exits 1
  while something is to do.

  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

### `choregos self`

The CLI itself: keep it in step with the instance

#### `choregos self update`

```text
Usage: choregos self update [OPTIONS]

  Replace this CLI with the instance's own build, for this OS and processor.

  The binary comes from the instance (`/downloads/cli/`), in the version it
  runs, and is checked against the sha256 of its manifest before it replaces
  the running one in a single rename. A CLI installed from Python packages has
  no binary to replace: upgrade the package, or install the binary with the
  instance's install script.

Options:
  --api-url <str>  The instance to update from (default: the profile's)
  --path <path>    The binary to replace (default: the running one)
  --force          Download even when the versions are the same
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `choregos tokens`

```text
Usage: choregos tokens create [OPTIONS]

  Issue an API token for the caller. The secret is shown HERE, once.

Options:
  --name <str>             [required]
  --expires-in-days <int>  [default: 90]
  --scope <str>            `*` (REST API and CLI, the default), `mcp:read` /
                           `mcp:write` (MCP gate), or `a2a` (A2A door)
  --project <str>          `org:slug`: limits an MCP or A2A token to one
                           project
  --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

#### `choregos workflow push`

```text
Usage: choregos workflow push [OPTIONS] {project} [path]

  Publish the next version of a workflow, under the name its `metadata.name`
  gives.

  The project's other workflows do not move, and a work item in progress
  finishes on its version.

Arguments:
  project  [required]
  path     [default: .choregos/workflow.yaml]

                        replaced it
  --help                Show this message and exit.
```

```text
  plain words.

Arguments:

Options:
  --mermaid
  --process  each transition in plain words
  --help     Show this message and exit.
```

```text
  offline.

Arguments:
  path  [default: .choregos/workflow.yaml]

Options:
  --remote  validate through the API rather than locally
  --help    Show this message and exit.
```

## Concepts

This page explains the ideas behind every screen of Choregos. Read it once before your first
project; come back to it when a word in the console is unclear.

**What you will be able to do**

- Name the objects you meet in the console and say what each one is for.
- Tell who acts at each step of a workflow: an agent, a person or the platform.
- Know what protects a run, what it costs, and where its trace is kept.

### The big picture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph org["Organisation"]
    direction LR
    subgraph project["Project billing-api"]
      direction TB
      wi["Work item<br/>Export invoices as CSV"] --> wf["Workflow<br/>states and transitions"]
      wf --> stage["Stage: one transition"]
      stage -->|agent| run["Run<br/>sandbox, budget, token"]
      stage -->|human| decision["Decision<br/>approve, send back, answer"]
      stage -->|system| platform["Platform action<br/>open or merge a pull request"]
      run --> gates["Gates check the evidence"]
      gates -->|pass| wf
    end
    agents["Agents<br/>skills, tools, knowledge"] -.-> run
    connectors["Connectors<br/>GitHub, Jira, Slack"] -.-> project
    policy["Policy and budgets"] -.-> run
  end
  run --> journal["Journal, evidence, cost ledger, audit"]
  decision --> journal
```

A **work item** enters a **project**. The project's **workflow** says which step comes next and who
does it. An agent step is a **run**, checked by **gates**. A person's step is a **decision**. Everything
lands in the journal and the cost ledger.

### Organisation

The organisation is your company or team on a Choregos instance. It holds the projects, the people,
the agents, the skills, the knowledge bases and the connectors that projects share. An organisation
administrator manages it under **Admin**.

The community edition holds one organisation per instance. See [Editions](#editions).

### Project

A project is one stream of work with its own workflows, members, connectors, policy and budgets: a
repository a team develops (`billing-api`), or a business process with no code at all (an employee
onboarding). A project is often born from a **template**, which brings its workflows, its policy and
the agents those workflows name, and sets up the outside systems (labels, a board, webhooks).

A project tells you what it still lacks to run: its **readiness** list, on the first page of its
**Settings**, says what is missing and who can fix it.

### Members and roles

A person belongs to the organisation with a role, and may have a role on a project too. A project role
**adds** to the organisation role; it never takes anything away.

| Role | What it adds |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Viewer** | Read the project: its board, work items, runs and costs |
| **Developer** | Decide the human steps addressed to them, pause, resume, stop or replay work, triage findings, keep personal agents |
| **Release captain** | What a developer does, plus operate release trains and approve a production departure |
| **Project owner** | What a developer does, plus change the project: its settings, connectors, workflows, policy, models, members, its own agents and knowledge bases |
| **Organisation admin** | Everything, in every project: create projects, manage organisation agents, skills, connectors, models, the network and the audit log |

People also carry **groups** from your identity provider (for example `maintainers` or
`product-owners`). A workflow addresses a human step to a group; only a member of that group (or an
organisation administrator, and that override is audited) may answer it.

### Workflow

A workflow is the process a project follows, written as a state machine in YAML:

- **States** are the columns of the board: "To triage", "Specification to approve", "Merged". A state
  of kind `wait` waits for a person. A `terminal` state ends the work item.
- **Transitions** move a work item from one state to the next. Each transition names **who acts**
  (`by`), what it reads and produces (`inputs`, `outputs`), the **gates** that must pass, and what
  happens when it fails (`on_fail`: retry a few times, then escalate to a person).

Who acts on a transition:

| Actor | What it is |
| :-- | :-- |
| `agent` | An agent from the registry does the step, in a sandbox, under a budget |
| `human` | A person of a group decides: approve, send back, answer, or complete a task |
| `system` | The platform does it itself, at no model cost: open the pull request, merge it, open child work items |
| `job` | A fixed command runs in the sandbox, with no model: a backtest, a conversion |
| `decision` | A small model answers typed questions (finished? which team?) to choose the next step |

A workflow is **validated when it is written**, not when a work item is halfway through it: an
unreachable state, a retry that could loop forever or a gate with nothing to check is refused at once.
A workflow is **versioned**: publishing a change creates the next version, and a work item already in
progress finishes on the version it started with. A project may have several workflows; **routing**
rules (by label, by type) choose one for each incoming work item.

### Work item

A work item is one request: an issue on GitHub or GitLab, a Jira ticket, or a request filed in Choregos
itself. It is pinned to one version of one workflow when it starts. Its page shows where it is, what
it waits for, its journey, its cost per stage and what each step produced (its **artifacts**: a
specification, a report, a deck).

### Stage and run

A **stage** is one transition being carried out. When an agent carries it, the stage is a **run**:

- one disposable sandbox and one workspace (a clone of the repository when the agent needs one);
- one short-lived token, valid for that run only;
- one model key, capped at what is left of the budget;
- only the tools, knowledge and network the agent and its project allow.

The runner talks to the agent, records every message in the run's **journal**, applies the guard rails
(allowed paths, forbidden commands, network), and hands the result to the gates. A run that is played
again does not pay twice and does not act twice.

### Gates

A gate is a check the platform runs on what a step produced. It is code, not an instruction to the
agent. A few examples:

| Gate | Passes when |
| :-- | :-- |
| `evidence_present` | the tests were actually run by the platform, not just reported |
| `scope_respected` | the diff stays inside the paths the work item allows |
| `no_secrets` | the change writes no secret |
| `outputs_present` | the step produced every output the transition declares |
| `ci_green` | the pull request's checks are green |
| `docs_updated` | a change to the code also changes the documentation |

**A gate that cannot see what it must check refuses.** A guarantee that passes blindly is worse than
none. The [workflow reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/concepts.md#gate) lists every gate.

### Agents

An agent is a registered, versioned object of the organisation: its instructions, the model it uses,
its skills, its tools, the knowledge it reads, its limits. Each change publishes a new **version**; a
project runs the version its **production** channel points to, and a new version can be tried on a
**testing** channel first.

An agent has an **owner**: the common catalogue (installed with the platform), the organisation, one
project, or one person. A **personal** agent never runs in a workflow: a process the whole team relies
on must not depend on an agent one person can change or take away.

Agents come in several kinds:

| Kind | What it is |
| :-- | :-- |
| Coding agent | A coding agent the runner ships (Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and others), working in the workspace |
| Prompt agent | Instructions, a model, tools and knowledge, with no coding agent: the platform runs the tool loop |
| Voice agent | The same, spoken: a realtime model and a voice, used in sessions, never as a workflow step |
| Hosted agent | Your own container, following a standard contract |
| Code agent | An agent written in code (LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, plain Python), in an image built from the runner's |
| Remote agent | An agent elsewhere, called over A2A (for example Atlassian Rovo), under the same gates and budget |

See [Agents](build/agents.md) for how to create them.

### Skills

A skill is a folder of know-how an agent loads: how to write a decision record, how your team names
branches, the checklist of a security review. Skills are a library of the organisation, versioned like
agents. **A skill grants no permission**: what an agent may call is decided by its version and its
project, never by a file it reads. See [Skills](build/skills.md).

### Tools and MCP servers

An agent's own tools are those of its coding agent (read a file, run a command). On top of them, the
platform offers:

- **its own tools**, always there: report a finding outside the agent's scope, ask a person a question,
  request a wider scope;
- **catalogue tools**: a short list of third-party APIs and **MCP servers** the organisation chose.
  The platform calls them on the agent's behalf: the agent never holds the credential, never chooses
  the address and never sees the remote tool's real name. A tool the agent may not use answers "not
  found", like a tool that does not exist.

An agent version names the tools it uses; its project can only narrow that list, never widen it. See
[Tools](build/tools.md).

### Knowledge bases and memory

A **knowledge base** is a set of documents a person curates and agents only read: an architecture
framework, policies, runbooks, a product's documentation. Its documents are uploaded or synced from
Confluence, SharePoint, a git repository or a web site, and converted to text. Its **reach** says which
projects' runs are served it; its **grants** say who may change it. See [Knowledge](use/knowledge.md).

**Memory** is different: what agents learn from work, proposed by runs and accepted by people.

### Connectors

A connector is how Choregos talks to an outside system: the **tracker** where requests live (GitHub
Issues, Jira, GitLab, or Choregos itself), the **repository** (GitHub), the **deployment** (Argo CD),
**notifications** (Slack, e-mail), documents, an identity directory. A **connector type** is an entry
of the catalogue; a **connector** is one the organisation or a project has installed and configured.
A project needs only what its workflows read, and its settings say which ones. See
[Connectors](use/connectors.md).

### Human decisions

A workflow names the points where a person decides. Choregos never guesses past them:

- an **approval**: approve, or send back with a reason;
- a **question** an agent asked: answer it, and the work resumes where it stopped;
- a **task** a person does in the real world: fill in a form, attest it was done;
- a **governed action**: a write into another system (create an account, order a laptop), proposed
  by an agent or a workflow and run by the platform only after the people it names approve.

Every human step has a deadline and an escalation. What waits for you is in the **Inbox**. See
[Decisions](use/decisions.md).

### Evidence, journal and audit

Choregos keeps three kinds of trace:

- **Evidence**: what a step measured and left behind: tests run and passed, lint, coverage, diff size,
  and the business **facts** a workflow names. Gates read it; the run page shows it, marked as
  observed by the platform or declared by the agent.
- **The journal** of each run: every message between the runner and the agent, what it read, wrote and
  ran, what it reached on the network, and what was refused.
- **The audit log** of the organisation (**Admin › Audit**): who changed a setting, approved a
  decision, granted a budget top-up, overrode a group.

### Budgets and policies

Every model call is made with a key capped for that run, and lands in a **cost ledger** with its
project, work item, stage and model. A run's key is minted at what is **left**: of its stage budget,
its work item's budget, its project's day and its organisation's month. When the money is spent, the
run stops and a person decides; a stage stopped on budget is never retried on its own.

A project's **policy** bounds what its agents may do: budgets by work item size, the paths no run may
write, forbidden commands, the hosts a run may reach, release trains. An organisation sets a
**ceiling** that every project policy can only tighten. See
[Budgets and policies](use/budgets-and-policies.md).

### Tokens and applications

- A **personal access token** lets you use the API and the command line as yourself. You create it
  under **My account › Access tokens**. Its **scope** limits what it opens: `*` (the API and the CLI),
  `mcp:read` or `mcp:write` (an AI assistant at the MCP door), or `a2a` (the A2A door). An MCP or A2A
  token can be limited to one project. A token is shown once, expires, and can be revoked.
- An **application** (a machine account) is how another system calls Choregos under its own name, not
  a person's. It belongs to one project (**Settings › People › Applications**), has its own daily
  budget, and outlives the person who created it. An application starts work; it never takes a
  decision.

### Editions

- The **community edition** is Apache 2.0 and holds one organisation per instance. Everything in this
  documentation is in it.
- The **enterprise edition** is published separately. It adds several organisations on one instance,
  with the isolation and the identity features they need.

**Admin › Edition** and **About** (at the bottom of the sidebar) say which one runs.

### Go further

- [Get started](get-started.md): try it, then run a first project.
- [Concepts in depth](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/concepts.md), the reference page these concepts come from.
- [Where Choregos sits](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/positioning.md) against other agent platforms, runtimes and tool brokers.

---

## Get started

This page has two parts. First, try Choregos on your own machine: one command, nothing to configure,
a demo work item waiting for your approval. Then run a real development project end to end: create it
from a template, connect its repository, open an issue, let agents work, approve, merge.

**What you will be able to do**

- Run Choregos locally and approve your first work item.
- Create a development project from the `github-software-delivery` template.
- Send an issue through the workflow and take the decisions it asks of you.

### Part 1: try it on your machine

#### Before you start

- Docker with Compose, and about 2 GB of free memory.
- Git, to fetch the source.
- No model key: without one, agents are simulated and cost nothing. Everything else is real: the
  orchestrator, the database, the gates, the human decision.

#### Steps

1. Fetch the source and start everything:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos.git
   cd choregos
   cp .env.example .env
   docker compose up
   ```

   The first start builds the images and pulls the others. Count a few minutes, more on a slow
   connection.

2. Open **http://localhost:3000**. The sign-in page shows a development sign-in with the demo
   administrator, `admin@choregos.local`, already filled in. Press **Enter**.

3. You land on the **demo** project. Open **Board** in the sidebar. One work item, "Plan the team
   offsite", waits in the column **Plan to approve**: an agent has written a plan.

4. Open the work item. The **Decision awaited** card shows what is asked. Read the plan in
   **Artifacts**, then press **Approve**. To see the other path, type a reason and press **Send back**
   instead: the work item goes back to the agent with your reason.

#### What you should see

- After **Approve**, the work item moves to **Approved**, a terminal state, and its **Journey** draws
  each step: the agent's plan, then your decision.
- On the run page (open the agent's step from the journey), the summary says that no model ran. That
  is the simulated mode.

#### What can go wrong

| Symptom | What to do |
| :-- | :-- |
| A port is already in use | Set `CHOREGOS_PORT_WEB` or `CHOREGOS_PORT_API` in `.env`, then start again |
| The console does not answer after several minutes | Run `docker compose ps`: the one-shot services (the migrations, the seed) have exited, every other one is healthy |
| You want real agents | Put an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env` and start again; see the [local install in depth](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/getting-started.md#fakes-mode-and-a-real-model) |

This install is for a laptop only. With a model key, the workers start agent containers through the
Docker socket, which amounts to root on the machine. To stop everything and delete the data:

```bash
docker compose down -v
```

### Part 2: a real development project

The running example of this documentation: the team behind `acme/billing-api` wants agents to take
features from an issue to production, with a person deciding at the points that matter. They use the
`github-software-delivery` template, which brings three workflows:

| Workflow | For | People who decide |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `dev-simple` | a bug or a small fix (labels `bug`, `fix`, `chore`) | none, unless something goes wrong |
| `study` | a study that ends with one decision record (labels `study`, `adr`, `spike`) | the architects |
| `dev-complex` | a feature (labels `feature`, `epic`, `complex`) | a product owner on the specification, a maintainer on the pull request, a release captain on production |

#### Before you start

- **An instance of Choregos** your organisation runs. To install one, see
  [Host Choregos](host/index.md).
- **The organisation admin role.** Only an organisation administrator creates a project. Ask one if
  you are not.
- **The Choregos GitHub App installed** on the repository's owner. You can do it from the console, on
  the way (step 4).
- **Groups from your identity provider** for the people who decide: `product-owners`, `maintainers`,
  `release-captains` and `architects`. A human step is answered only by a member of its group.
- **A deployment connector** for the release train: Argo CD for real, or the `demo` type for a trial
  where nothing is deployed.
- **Branch protection** on the repository's default branch: required status checks, but no required
  review. People decide in Choregos; the platform merges.

#### 1. Create the project

In the console:

1. Open **Projects** in the sidebar and press **New project**.
2. Under **What does this project deliver?**, choose **Software, from a code repository**. Under
   **Stack template**, choose **GitHub · software delivery (fix, study, feature)**. Press **Next**.
3. Fill in **Identifier (slug)** with `billing-api`, **Display name** with "Billing API",
   **Repository** with `acme/billing-api`, and the **Main language**. Press **Next**.
4. Under **Tracker (where tickets come from)**, choose **GitHub Issues / Projects**. Press **Next**.
5. Check the summary and press **Create and provision**.

Or from the command line, once you are signed in (see [Install the CLI](cli/install.md)):

```bash
choregos login --api-url https://choregos.example.com --token chg_xxx --org acme
choregos projects create billing-api --name "Billing API" --repo https://github.com/acme/billing-api --template github-software-delivery
choregos projects provision billing-api --follow
```

Provisioning creates the routing labels (`bug`, `feature`, `study` and the others) and the webhooks on
the repository, and installs the template's workflows, policy and agents. It is safe to run again: it
resumes where it stopped.

#### 2. Finish the setup with the readiness list

Open the project's **Settings**. The readiness list at the top says what the project still lacks, item
by item, and who can fix each one. Work through it:

1. **Settings › Connections**: the **Source code** card shows "The Choregos App is not installed" until
   the App is there; press **Install on GitHub**, install it on the repository, and come back. Press
   **Test** on each card until it reads **Connected**.
2. On the **Deployment (CD)** card, press **Configure** and choose Argo CD, or `demo` for a trial.
3. **Settings › People**: make sure someone holds the **Project owner** role, and someone the
   **Release captain** role. See [Projects and members](use/projects-and-members.md).
4. **Settings › General**: set the command that proves production is healthy (a `smoke_ok` fact, for
   example a `curl` on the health page). The production check fails without it.

The same list, from the command line (it exits with 1 while something is left to do):

```bash
choregos projects readiness billing-api
```

#### 3. Open the first work item

On GitHub, open an issue on `acme/billing-api`: "Export invoices as CSV", with a description of what
you expect. Add two labels: `feature` (it routes the issue to `dev-complex`) and `agent-ready` (it
starts the work). Nothing starts without `agent-ready`.

Within a minute, the work item appears on the project's **Board**, and the issue gets a status comment
that Choregos keeps up to date.

#### 4. Follow the agents

Open the work item from the board. Its **Journey** shows the workflow as a path: a circle for an agent
step, a circle with a person for a decision, a square for the platform. The current step pulses.

The triager sizes the issue, then the specification writer writes a specification with criteria that
can be checked and the paths the change may touch. Open a step to see its run: its cost, its evidence,
what it read and wrote, and its live journal.

#### 5. Approve the specification

The work item stops in **Specification to approve** and appears in the **Inbox** of the
`product-owners`. As one of them:

1. Open the work item. Read the specification in **Artifacts**.
2. Press **Approve**. Or write what is wrong and press **Send back**: the specification writer starts
   again with your reason.

#### 6. Let it be built, then approve the pull request

Agents plan, implement, test, document and review the change. After each step, gates check the
result: the tests really ran, the diff stays in the allowed paths, no secret was written, the
documentation changed with the code. A failed check sends the work back to the agent a few times, then
to a person.

The platform then opens the pull request, and the work item waits in **Pull request to approve** for
the `maintainers`. Read the diff on GitHub or in the run's **Diff**, then press **Approve** in
Choregos. When the repository's checks are green, the platform merges the pull request and the work
item reaches **Merged**.

#### 7. Release

The release train takes the change to staging, then waits for a release captain to approve the
production departure (see [Decisions](use/decisions.md)). After the release, an agent checks
production from measured facts, and the work item ends in **Verified in production**.

#### What you should see

- On the issue: a status comment with the state, the cost so far and a link to the work item.
- On the work item's page: every step of the journey green, the cost per stage, the artifacts (the
  specification, the plan, the test report, the release notes).
- In **Spend**: what the work item cost, by agent and by model.

#### What can go wrong

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The issue is labelled but nothing appears | The App is not installed, or the webhook does not reach the instance | **Settings › Connections**: test the cards; a periodic catch-up also picks up labelled issues |
| The work item went to `dev-simple` | The `feature` label was missing | Open the work item and press **Change workflow** |
| "Only its members answer it" when you approve | You are not in the step's group at your last sign-in | Ask your identity provider administrator; an organisation admin can answer instead, and it is audited |
| The work item is in **Needs a human** | A step failed its gates too many times, an agent asked a question, or the budget ran out | Read the step's run, then answer, replay the stage or stop the work item: see [Work items](use/work-items.md) |
| The merge never happens | A required check is red, or the merge queue setting does not match the repository | Read the pull request's checks; set the source code connector's merge queue option to match |

### Go further

- [Concepts](concepts.md), if a word on this page was new.
- [Work items](use/work-items.md) and [Decisions](use/decisions.md), for the daily work.
- [Workflows](use/workflows.md), to change the process the template brought.
- The [template's own page](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/templates/github-software-delivery/README.md), for every detail of its
  three workflows.

---

## Backups and restore

**What you will be able to do:** know what an instance cannot lose, back it up, and restore it.

### What to back up

| What | Why | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The platform database** (PostgreSQL) | projects, work items, decisions, the journal, the cost ledger, sealed secrets | continuous archiving with point-in-time recovery; with CloudNativePG, a target of 5 minutes of data at most |
| **Temporal's database** | where each work item in flight stands | the same tool and the same frequency as the platform database |
| **The object store** | the file artefacts of runs (documents, spreadsheets, images) | your object store's versioning or replication |
| **The `secrets-keks` key** | without it, every connector secret in the database is unreadable | in your vault, with the vault's own backups; keep old keys while a backup sealed with them can still be restored |
| **Your Helm values and Secrets' source** | to rebuild the instance | in git and in your vault |

**Restore the platform database and Temporal's to the same instant.** A work item whose position in
Temporal and in the platform database disagree is stuck or replays a step.

### Restore

1. Restore PostgreSQL into a **new** cluster at the chosen instant, then point
   `global.database.secretRef` at it:
   [PostgreSQL restore runbook](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/postgres-restore.md).
2. Restore Temporal's database to the same instant:
   [Temporal backup runbook](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/temporal-backup.md).
3. Restart the API and the workers, then list the workflows Temporal runs and compare them with the
   work items the console shows in progress. The Temporal runbook says how to start again a work item
   that lost its workflow.

### Purging

The database grows with runs, events and transcripts; the
[purge runbook](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/purge-runs.md)
says what can go, and keeps what the audit needs.

---

## Identity

People sign in to Choregos through your identity provider, and their roles come from its groups. No
password is stored by Choregos.

**What you will be able to do:** register Choregos at your identity provider, map groups to roles,
and let claude.ai or Claude Code sign in to the MCP door with single sign-on.

### 1. Register the client

At your identity provider, register a **confidential** client:

- redirect URI: `https://choregos.example.com/api/v1/auth/callback` (your `apiUrl` followed by
  `/api/v1/auth/callback`);
- scopes: `openid profile email groups`;
- a `groups` claim in the userinfo answer, and `sub` and `email`.

Put its secret in a Secret under the key `client-secret`, and point the chart at it:

```yaml
global:
  oidc:
    issuer: https://sso.example.com/realms/acme
    clientId: choregos
    secretRef: choregos-oidc
```

The provider must publish a discovery document whose `issuer` equals `global.oidc.issuer`. Choregos
signs in with PKCE, a single-use `state` and a `nonce`. A person is bound to their `sub`: a changed
e-mail keeps the account. **Admin › Identity** shows what the instance reads (issuer, client, redirect
URI to register, whether the secret is set), never a secret's value.

### 2. Give roles through groups

| Group at the identity provider | Role in Choregos |
| --- | --- |
| `choregos:<org>:org-admins` | `org_admin` of the organisation |
| `choregos:<org>:product-owners` | `project_owner` |
| `choregos:<org>:release-captains` | `release_captain` |
| `choregos:<org>:developers` | `developer` |
| `choregos:<org>:viewers` | `viewer` |

The same claim carries the human groups workflows name: a step for `group: architects` is offered to
members carrying `architects` or `choregos:acme:architects`. Groups without the `choregos:<org>:`
prefix count only when `global.oidc.defaultOrg` names the organisation.

The first administrators come from `global.bootstrap.admins` ([Install](install.md#1-write-your-values)).

### Signing in to the MCP door with OAuth

claude.ai, Claude on mobile and ChatGPT call the MCP door from their vendor's cloud and sign in with
OAuth; Claude Code can too, instead of a pasted token. The door becomes an OAuth resource server with:

```yaml
global:
  mcp:
    oauth:
      enabled: true
      audience: choregos-mcp
      clients:
        claude-code: { clientId: choregos-claude-code, callbackPort: 33418 }
        claude-ai: { clientId: choregos-claude-ai }
```

- `audience` is the audience your provider puts in the door's tokens: a token issued for another
  application does not open the door.
- `clients` names the clients you registered at your provider, by the console's names
  (`claude-code`, `claude-desktop`, `claude-ai`, `cursor`, `vscode`, `chatgpt`, `other`): the
  Integrations page then shows each one's exact setup. An unknown name stops the API at start-up.
- `issuer` is empty by default: the console's own issuer.

The door publishes `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`. For claude.ai and ChatGPT, it and
`/mcp` must be reachable on a public HTTPS address. A person must have signed in to the console once
before the door knows them. Setting up Keycloak for it:
[runbook](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/keycloak-mcp.md).

### What can go wrong

| Symptom | Likely cause |
| --- | --- |
| sign-in answers `503` | the discovery document cannot be read, or its `issuer` differs from `global.oidc.issuer` |
| sign-in answers `401` | the ID token's issuer, audience or nonce does not match the sign-in |
| a person signs in with no role | no `choregos:<org>:…` group, or an unprefixed group without `defaultOrg` |
| an existing account is not linked | the provider says `email_verified: false` |
| `401 invalid_token` at the MCP door with OAuth | a wrong audience or issuer, or keys the provider no longer publishes |

Everything about identity, including moving to a new provider and per-organisation providers:
[deployment reference, Identity](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/deployment.md#identity-what-the-oidc-provider-must-give-us).

---

## Host Choregos

These pages are for the people who run a Choregos instance on Kubernetes. They are a digest: each one
says what to do and links to the full
[deployment reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/deployment.md) for
every value and every edge case.

**What you will be able to do:** install an instance with Helm, connect it to your identity provider,
provide its secrets, upgrade it, back it up, and know what protects what.

### What you run

| Component | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **API** (`choregos-api`) | the REST API, the MCP and A2A doors, webhooks, sign-in; the only component that reads the object store |
| **Console** (`choregos-web`) | the web interface |
| **Orchestrator workers** (`choregos-orchestrator`) | the Temporal workers that move work items and start agent runs, one deployment per queue |
| **Tools** (`choregos-tools`) | the platform's MCP tool server for runs |
| **Runner** | the image every agent run starts in, one sandboxed pod per run |

They depend on PostgreSQL, Temporal, a model gateway (LiteLLM), an S3-compatible object store and an
OIDC identity provider. Each dependency can be embedded by the chart, for a bench, or external, for
production (the default).

### Prerequisites

| Need | Minimum | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kubernetes | 1.24 | 1.29 for hosted agents, which run as native sidecars |
| Helm | 3.12 | the chart is published as an OCI artifact |
| PostgreSQL | 15 | an operator such as CloudNativePG in production; the API must not connect as a superuser |
| Temporal | 1.22 | a cluster in production |
| An OIDC provider | | any issuer with a discovery document; Keycloak in our deployments |
| The agent-sandbox operator | v1.0.6 | backs the default executor; the chart does not render without its CRDs |
| An S3-compatible object store | | for file artefacts; AWS S3, MinIO, RustFS |
| An ingress | | Gateway API `HTTPRoute` by default, or a classic `Ingress` |
| External Secrets Operator | | used by default to bring the API's secrets from your vault; can be turned off |
| Kyverno | 1.12 | for the admission policies shipped in `infra/policies` |

Recommended in production: a model gateway with real provider keys (cost is measured and capped
there), gVisor as a `RuntimeClass` for agent pods, and a memory service (Ecphoria).

### Try it on your machine first

To see Choregos before installing it on a cluster, run it with Docker Compose from the repository:
`git clone https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos.git`, `cp .env.example .env`, then
`docker compose up`, and open `http://localhost:3000`. It listens on `127.0.0.1` only and is not a
deployment.

### The pages

1. [Install with Helm](install.md): the chart, a first values file, the first organisation and token.
2. [Identity](identity.md): single sign-on, roles from your identity provider's groups, OAuth for the
   MCP door.
3. [Secrets](secrets.md): what the chart expects, and the key that seals connector secrets.
4. [Upgrades](upgrades.md): the order of operations, migrations, what to read before.
5. [Backups and restore](backups.md): what to back up, and restoring to one instant.
6. [Security model](security.md): what protects what, and what does not.
7. [Runbooks](runbooks.md): the short list for when something goes wrong.

---

## Install with Helm

**What you will be able to do:** install an instance, sign in, and hand the first token to a person.

**Before you start:** the [prerequisites](index.md#prerequisites) in place, and the
[secrets](secrets.md) created in the namespace (or in your vault, with External Secrets).

### 1. Write your values

A first `my-values.yaml` for an instance at `https://choregos.example.com`, with external
dependencies:

```yaml
global:
  environment: prod
  publicUrl: https://choregos.example.com
  apiUrl: https://choregos.example.com
  database:
    host: choregos-pg-rw.choregos-data.svc
    name: choregos
    user: choregos
    secretRef: choregos-db
  temporal:
    address: temporal-frontend.choregos-temporal.svc:7233
  gateway:
    url: http://litellm.choregos-gateway.svc:4000
    secretRef: choregos-gateway-secrets
  objectStore:
    url: s3://choregos-artefacts
    secretRef: choregos-object-store
  oidc:
    issuer: https://sso.example.com/realms/acme
    clientId: choregos
    secretRef: choregos-oidc
  bootstrap:
    org: acme
    orgName: ACME
    admins: "alice@acme.example,bob@acme.example"
choregos-api:
  ingress:
    hostnames: ["choregos.example.com"]
choregos-web:
  ingress:
    hostnames: ["choregos.example.com"]
```

- `publicUrl` and `apiUrl` are what the API builds every address from: the sign-in callback, the
  Integrations page's commands, the links in notifications. Set both to `https://…`.
- `bootstrap` creates the first organisation and makes those people its administrators at every
  start, never changing what exists. There is no default organisation.
- In `staging` and `prod`, the chart refuses to render with an embedded dependency, generated
  secrets, the development sign-in or the demonstration fakes.

For a single-node bench with every dependency embedded, start from the chart's
`values/local.yaml` overlay instead.

### 2. Install

```shell
helm upgrade --install choregos oci://ghcr.io/vargafoundation/charts/choregos \
  --version 0.26.1 --namespace choregos --create-namespace -f my-values.yaml
```

The chart's version is the product's version; the images
(`ghcr.io/vargafoundation/choregos-api`, `-web`, `-orchestrator`, `-tools`, `-runner`) follow it, are
multi-arch and signed. The database migrations run as a Helm hook before the API starts.

Install the admission policies once per cluster, from a checkout of the repository at the same tag:

```shell
kubectl apply -k infra/policies
```

### 3. Check it

```shell
kubectl -n choregos get pods
curl -s https://choregos.example.com/healthz
```

**What you should see:** the API, the console and the worker deployments `Running`, and
`{"status":"ok"}`. Open `https://choregos.example.com` and sign in as one of the `bootstrap.admins`.

### 4. The first token

Once signed in, a person creates their own tokens (**My account**, or `choregos tokens create`).
Before anyone has signed in, the first one comes from the server side:

```shell
kubectl -n choregos exec deploy/choregos-api -- choregos-admin tokens create --email alice@acme.example
choregos login --api-url https://choregos.example.com --token chg_... --org acme
```

### What can go wrong

| Symptom | Likely cause |
| --- | --- |
| the render fails naming `agent-sandbox` | the agent-sandbox operator's CRDs are missing |
| the API does not start, naming `CHOREGOS_SESSION_SECRET` | the session secret is missing or shorter than 32 bytes |
| every agent call answers `Signature verification failed` | the orchestrator and the API do not share `run-token-private-key` |
| sign-in answers `503` | the identity provider's discovery document cannot be read, or names another issuer |
| sign-in loops back to the login page | the URLs say `https` but the ingress also serves plain HTTP: redirect it |
| the first run that writes a file fails | the object store has no credentials or a wrong endpoint |

The full list of values: the
[deployment reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/deployment.md).

---

## Runbooks

Each runbook starts from a symptom and ends with how to check it is fixed. They live in the
repository, next to the alerts that link to them.

| Symptom | Runbook |
| --- | --- |
| the API answers 5xx | [The API returns 5xx](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/api-5xx.md) |
| a run stays `Pending` or never ends | [A run stays Pending or never ends](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/stuck-run.md) |
| a ticket labelled for an agent did not start | [An agent-ready ticket did not start](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/lost-webhook.md) |
| a release train is frozen | [A train is frozen and nothing departs](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/train-frozen.md) |
| a node was lost | [Losing a node](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/node-loss.md) |
| the database must be restored | [Restoring PostgreSQL](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/postgres-restore.md) |
| Temporal must be backed up, restored or upgraded | [Temporal: what to back up](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/temporal-backup.md), [Upgrading Temporal](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/temporal-upgrade.md) |
| a secret must be rotated | [Rotating secrets](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/secret-rotation.md) |
| the database keeps growing | [Purging runs, events and transcripts](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/purge-runs.md) |
| the MCP gateway is down or refusing | [The MCP gateway is down](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/mcp-gateway-down.md) |
| claude.ai cannot sign in to the MCP door | [Signing in to the MCP door with Keycloak](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/keycloak-mcp.md) |
| the memory service lost its quorum | [Ecphoria lost its Raft quorum](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/ecphoria-quorum.md) |

The full index: [runbooks](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/README.md).

## Secrets

The chart never writes production secrets: it expects them in the namespace, created by hand or
brought from your vault by the External Secrets Operator (on by default, from the
`ClusterSecretStore` named by `global.externalSecrets.storeRef`).

**What you will be able to do:** create every secret the instance needs, and rotate them.

### What the instance reads

| Secret | Keys | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `choregos-api-secrets` (`global.apiSecretRef`) | `session-secret`, `run-token-private-key`; optional `run-token-public-key`, `session-secret-previous`, `secrets-keks` | API; the run-token key and `secrets-keks` by the orchestrator too |
| the same, for GitHub | `github-app-id`, `github-app-private-key`, `github-webhook-secret`; optional `github-app-client-id`, `github-app-client-secret` | API and orchestrator |
| `global.oidc.secretRef` | `client-secret` | API |
| `global.database.secretRef` | `url` | API, orchestrator |
| `global.gateway.secretRef` | `master-key` | orchestrator |
| `global.objectStore.secretRef` | `access-key`, `secret-key` | API |
| `global.memory.tokenSecret` | `token` | orchestrator |

### Generate them

```shell
openssl rand -base64 48
openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout
python3 -c "import os,base64;print('k1:'+base64.b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode())"
```

- **`session-secret`** (the first command) signs the session cookie and the sign-in handshakes. It is
  required; on a deployed instance it must be at least 32 bytes.
- **`run-token-private-key`** (the second) signs the tokens of agent runs: the orchestrator mints
  them, the API checks them, so **both** must read the same key.
- **`secrets-keks`** (the third) seals the connector secrets people type in the console. Without it,
  typing a secret answers `409`.

```shell
kubectl -n choregos create secret generic choregos-api-secrets \
  --from-literal=session-secret="$SESSION_SECRET" \
  --from-file=run-token-private-key=run-token.pem \
  --from-literal=secrets-keks="$KEKS"
```

With External Secrets, put the same properties under `choregos/api` in your vault; add
`global.secrets.keksInExternalSecret: true` once `secrets-keks` exists there.

### The key that seals connector secrets

`secrets-keks` is a list `id:base64`, the first entry sealing and the others only opening. **Losing it
loses every sealed value**, and a database backup alone reveals none of them. Keep it in your vault,
backed up.

To rotate it: put the new key first (`k2:…,k1:…`), redeploy, run `choregos admin secrets rewrap` as
the platform administrator, and remove the old key only once no database backup older than the rewrap
can still be restored.

### Rotating the others

- **Session secret:** move the old value to `session-secret-previous`, put the new one in
  `session-secret`, redeploy, and remove the previous one after 8 hours.
- **Run-token key:** the API and the orchestrator read the same Secret, so both take the new key at
  their restart. A run started before can no longer post its result: rotate it in a quiet window, when
  no run is in flight.

The step-by-step:
[secret rotation runbook](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/secret-rotation.md).
`global.devSecrets: true` generates everything for a bench; it is refused in `staging` and `prod`.

---

## Security model

Choregos assumes **an agent may attempt anything**, by mistake or by injection, and that a member of
one organisation will try to read another's. This page is the digest; the full model, with what is
not guarded, is the
[security reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/security.md).

### Organisations are isolated in the database

Every request declares the organisations it may see, and PostgreSQL's row-level security refuses the
rest; a request that declares nothing sees nothing. That is why the API must connect as a role that
is **not** a superuser (a superuser ignores row-level security): in `staging` and `prod` it refuses to
start otherwise.

### Agents run in a sandbox

- One pod per run: non-root, no capabilities, a seccomp profile, no service-account token, required
  by the Kyverno policies in `infra/policies`. Set `global.runner.runtimeClass` to run every agent pod
  under gVisor or Kata; a project's policy can demand gVisor.
- A run holds only its own short-lived token. It never holds a provider key (the model gateway gets
  the run's own capped key), nor a connector's credential (the API calls tools for it).
- Writes outside the work item's allowed paths, and to the denied paths of the project's policy, are
  refused; the result is checked by the workflow's gates, not trusted.

### Network: three layers

1. The organisation's network list, which an administrator manages (**Admin › Network**), under a
   ceiling the operator sets (`global.egress.ceiling`).
2. A per-run egress proxy (`global.egress.enabled: true`), the wall for host, port and connection rate.
3. Your cluster's network policies.

The proxy cannot see inside TLS: methods, paths and headers are invisible to it. Allow hosts, not
URLs.

### Tokens and their scopes

| Scope | Opens | Never opens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `*` | the REST API and the CLI | the MCP and A2A doors |
| `mcp:read`, `mcp:write` | the MCP door, optionally one project | the REST API |
| `a2a` | the A2A door, optionally one project | the REST API |
| an application's token | the A2A door, on its project, 365 days at most | everything else |

Tokens are stored as digests and shown once. **A decision** (approving a specification, a merge, a
release) is taken by a person signed in to the console, never by a token, an MCP client or an A2A
caller, and the sensitive ones ask that person to sign in again.

### Secrets

Connector secrets typed in the console are sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key the deployment holds
(`secrets-keks`): a database dump reveals nothing, and losing the key loses the values
([Secrets](secrets.md)).

### Audit

Every sign-in, token, door call, decision and change of rights is in the audit log (**Admin ›
Audit**), under the same organisation isolation as the rest.

### Supply chain

The images are signed with cosign (keyless), with an SBOM and SLSA provenance attached; the Kyverno
policies can require digest references. Hosted agents' images can be required to carry a trusted
signature (`global.images.hostedCosign: enforce`).

### Reporting a vulnerability

Follow [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/SECURITY.md); do not
open a public issue.

---

## Upgrades

**What you will be able to do:** move an instance to a new version without losing work in flight.

### Before you upgrade

1. **Read the release notes** of every version between yours and the target, on the
   [GitHub releases](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/releases), and the "Upgrading to …"
   sections of the
   [deployment reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/deployment.md#upgrading-to-024).
   A breaking change says what to rename or set before you upgrade.
2. **Back up** the platform database and Temporal's, to the same instant ([Backups](backups.md)).
   The migrations change the schema; restoring a backup is the only way back.
3. Upgrade one minor version at a time when the notes say so.

### Upgrade

The same command as the install, with the new version:

```shell
helm upgrade --install choregos oci://ghcr.io/vargafoundation/charts/choregos \
  --version 0.26.1 --namespace choregos -f my-values.yaml
```

- The database migrations run as a Helm hook **before** the new API starts
  (`python -m choregos_api.migrate`, in a Job that waits for the database up to 300 seconds). With an
  embedded database the hook runs after the install instead: keep `choregos-api.migrations.hook` as
  the chart sets it.
- Work items in flight finish on the workflow version they started on; Temporal keeps their position
  across the restart of the workers.
- The images follow the chart's version.

### Check it

```shell
kubectl -n choregos get pods
kubectl -n choregos get jobs -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=choregos
curl -s https://choregos.example.com/api/v1/edition
```

**What you should see:** every pod `Running` on the new images, the job `choregos-migrations-<revision>`
completed, and the edition answer's `version` naming the new version.

### When it goes wrong

| Symptom | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| the migration Job fails | read its logs; the API did not start on the new version, the old pods still serve. Fix the cause, then run the upgrade again |
| the API refuses to start after the upgrade | its log names the setting; most often a value the release notes asked to change |
| you must go back | `helm rollback` restores the previous pods, not the previous schema: restore the database backup taken before the upgrade, then roll back |

Upgrading Temporal itself has its own
[runbook](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/runbooks/temporal-upgrade.md).

### Upgrading to 0.26

0.26 brings [assistants](../use/assistants.md): a plugin may ship one, an organisation installs it for
an audience, and people converse with it in the console, from an MCP client or in an embedded frame.
Nothing changes for an organisation that installs none. The migrations run with the chart's job as
usual. The full table is in the
[deployment reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/deployment.md#upgrading-to-026); what you do is:

1. **Bound the token exchange.** Set `CHOREGOS_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_AUDIENCES` to a JSON list of your sources'
   audiences (in `global.extraEnv`) before binding a need that uses the person's identity
   (`user_exchange`). Unset, a connector's editor chooses any audience the identity provider allows. See
   the [review of the person's identity](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/security.md).
2. **Prepare the identity provider.** `user_exchange` needs token exchange (RFC 8693) enabled for the
   API's client and limited to those audiences. A standing delegation needs `offline_access` with
   bounded, revocable offline sessions. See [Identity](identity.md).
3. **Give conversation suites a model.** An assistant's conversation suites gate the promotion of its
   agent version, and a judge model scores their rubrics (`conversation_judge_model`, else the `strong`
   model profile). With no gateway key, a version whose assistant ships suites is refused promotion
   with the reason. `conversation_suites_require_model=false` opts out, and no check then runs.
4. **Pick a quiet hour.** The migration that makes `/responses` sessions durable closes the ones open at
   upgrade time. Matters only if you use hosted prompt agents.
5. **List the host origins** of an embedded assistant in the installation's `config.embed_origins`; nothing
   else to deploy. Accounts connected before 0.26 are connected again once.

:::caution Delegated tasks
The standing delegation ships, but its decision record
([ADR 0137](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/adr/0137-a-standing-read-only-delegation.md)) stays proposed until the works council has
given its opinion and the data protection impact assessment is done. Do not offer delegated tasks to
people before then.
:::

---

## Choregos

**Choregos runs your team's work through agents and people, under rules you can check.** A request
comes in: an issue, a ticket, a form, a call from another system. Choregos moves it through a
**workflow** you declare. Agents do the steps they are given. People decide where the workflow says a
person decides. Every step has a budget it cannot exceed and leaves evidence you can read. Nothing
moves on because an agent says it is done: the platform checks.

Choregos is open source (Apache 2.0), self-hosted, and works with any agent. It is published by the
Varga Foundation.

### Who it is for

- **A team lead** who wants agents to take a share of the work without losing control of what ships:
  who approved it, what it cost, what it changed.
- **A developer** who files work, follows what an agent does, reviews its result and takes over when
  it gets stuck.
- **An operator or administrator** who connects the tools the team already uses (GitHub, Jira,
  Confluence, Slack, an identity provider), sets the budgets and decides what agents may reach.

It is not tied to software. The same engine carries an HR onboarding, a purchasing request or a data
change: anything that arrives as a request and is done in steps.

### What it is not

- **Not a chat.** Agents work unattended. People step in at the points the workflow names, with a
  deadline.
- **Not a coding agent.** Choregos runs the coding agents you choose, in disposable sandboxes, and
  gives them only what one step needs.
- **Not a promise in a prompt.** A check (a **gate**) is code: tests that really ran, a diff inside the
  allowed paths, the documents a step must produce. A gate that cannot see what it must check refuses.

### A five-minute tour

Here is the life of one request in a classic development project, `billing-api`, created from the
software-delivery template.

1. **A developer opens an issue** on GitHub, "Export invoices as CSV", and labels it `agent-ready`
   and `feature`. That label is the only trigger.
2. **Choregos picks the workflow.** The `feature` label routes it to the `dev-complex` workflow. The
   work item appears on the project's **Board**, in the first column.
3. **An agent triages it**, sizes it (S, M, L or XL) and estimates the risk. **Another agent writes
   the specification**, with criteria that can be checked.
4. **The work item waits for a person.** The specification goes to the product owners. It shows in
   the **Inbox** with a deadline. One of them reads it and presses **Approve**, or **Send back** with
   a reason; the agent then tries again with that reason.
5. **Agents plan, implement, test and document**, on a branch, inside the paths the specification
   allows. After each step a gate checks the result: the tests were really run, no secret was written,
   the diff stays in scope. A failed check sends the work back, a few times at most, then to a person.
6. **Agents review the change**, then the platform opens the pull request. A maintainer approves it
   in Choregos. When the repository's checks are green, the platform merges it.
7. **A release train deploys it**, first to staging, then to production after a release captain
   approves the departure. An agent checks production from measured facts.
8. **Everything stays readable.** The work item's page draws its journey, step by step. Each run shows
   its cost, its evidence, what the agent read, wrote and was refused, and its full log.

### How to read this documentation

Read it in order the first time: what it is, the ideas, a first project, then the daily tasks.

| Section | Read it to |
| :-- | :-- |
| [Concepts](concepts.md) | Learn the words: organisation, project, workflow, run, gate, evidence, budget |
| [Get started](get-started.md) | Try Choregos on your machine, then run a first real project end to end |
| **Use Choregos** | Do the daily work in the console |
| ▸ [Projects and members](use/projects-and-members.md) | Create a project, invite people, give them roles |
| ▸ [Workflows](use/workflows.md) | Choose, read, change and publish the process a project follows |
| ▸ [Work items](use/work-items.md) | File work, follow it, take over when it is stuck |

### Editions

This documentation describes the **community edition**: Apache 2.0, one organisation per instance,
everything in this documentation included. An **enterprise edition**, published separately, adds
several organisations on one instance and the identity features that come with them. The console
shows which edition runs under **About**, at the bottom of the sidebar.

### Where the deep detail lives

These pages are written for people who use Choregos. The complete reference, written for the people
who run and extend it, is in the repository: the [reference documentation](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/README.md), the
[concepts in depth](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/concepts.md), [usage in depth](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/usage.md), [security](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/security.md) and the
[architecture decisions](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.1/docs/adr/README.md). Where a page and the code disagree, the code is right and
the page is a bug: [report it](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/issues).

## Start a workflow over A2A

Your billing team's order system should be able to say "ship this change" to Choregos and get the
result back, without anyone opening the console. The **A2A door** does that: it serves your workflows
as skills of the [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org), versions **0.3.0** and **1.0**, as JSON-RPC
over HTTP. Any HTTP client can call it; the CLI's `choregos a2a` writes the JSON-RPC for you.

**What you will be able to do:** open a workflow to the door, give an application its own account
and token, list what it may start, start a work item with fields and a file, follow it to the end,
read its artefacts, cancel it, and be called back when it changes.

**Before you start:**

- a project with a workflow you can publish (here `acme:billing-api` and its `ship-a-change` workflow);
- the right to manage the project's members, to create an application's account;
- the CLI, [installed](../cli/install.md) and signed in, if you want the CLI side of each step;
- `curl` and, for one step, `jq`.

Every request of this page is sent to the real door by the test suite, in the page's order: a request
the door stops taking turns the build red.

:::note What the door never does
It never takes a human decision. When a step waits for a person, the task says so and gives the link
where that person decides, in the console. An application's token opens the A2A door and nothing
else: not the REST API, not the MCP door.
:::

### 1. Open the workflow to the door

Nothing is served by default: the door answers with an empty card until a workflow says `a2a:`. Add
the block, and say in `metadata.inputs` which fields the workflow takes, as a JSON Schema:

```yaml
metadata:
  name: ship-a-change
  version: 1
  inputs:
    type: object
    required: [ticket]
    properties:
      ticket: { type: string }
      priority: { type: string, enum: [low, high] }
a2a:
  skill: ship-a-change
  description: Ship a change through review and release.
  input_modes: [text/plain, application/json, application/pdf]
```

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `a2a.skill` | the skill's id; on the card it is `<project>/<skill>`, here `billing-api/ship-a-change` |
| `a2a.description` | what the caller's agent reads to choose the skill |
| `a2a.input_modes` | what the skill takes: `text/plain` for the request in words, `application/json` for the fields, a file's media type for that file; `[text/plain]` when absent |

Publish the workflow as usual, from the console (the workflow's **YAML** view) or with the CLI:

```bash
choregos workflow push acme:billing-api ship-a-change.yaml
```

The [workflow reference](../reference/workflow-yaml.md#a2a) lists every key.

### 2. Give the application its own account and token

An application should act under its own name: its account belongs to one project, keeps working when
the person who created it leaves, has its own daily budget (500 writes by default), and can never take
a decision. Its tokens open the A2A door only, on that project, and last 365 days at most.

**In the console:** open the project, then **Settings › People**, card **Applications**. Type the
application's name under *New application*, choose **Create**, then **Issue a token** on its line. The
token is shown once (*Token, shown once:*): copy it into the application's secret store.

**With the CLI:**

```bash
choregos machines create acme:billing-api partner-app --display-name "Partner app"
choregos machines token acme:billing-api partner-app --name production --expires-in-days 90
```

To rotate a token, issue the next one, switch the application to it, then revoke the old one with
`choregos machines revoke acme:billing-api partner-app <token id>` (`choregos machines list
acme:billing-api` shows the ids, never the values). **Remove** ends the application: its tokens stop
working at once.

**To try it as yourself first**, take a token that acts with your rights: the console's
**Integrations** page, card *Another agent, over A2A*, button **Create an A2A token** (30 days, shown
once), or:

```bash
choregos tokens create --name my-test --scope a2a --project acme:billing-api --expires-in-days 30
```

Keep both values at hand for the next steps:

```shell
export TOKEN=chg_...
export A2A=https://choregos.example.com/a2a/orgs/acme
```

The CLI finds the door from its profile (`choregos login`, or `CHOREGOS_API_URL` and `CHOREGOS_ORG`)
and takes the token from `--token` or `CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN`:

```shell
export CHOREGOS_API_URL=https://choregos.example.com CHOREGOS_ORG=acme CHOREGOS_A2A_TOKEN=chg_...
```

Without either, it sends the profile's own token, usually a full-access one, which the door refuses
with `403 insufficient_scope`; the CLI then tells you which token to create.

### 3. Read the card

The card lists the skills this token may start. It needs the token, since its content depends on who
asks.

```bash
curl -s "$A2A/.well-known/agent-card.json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

A skill that takes `application/json` also says which fields it wants, as the JSON Schema of its
`metadata.inputs`. A2A has no place for that on a skill, so it is in an optional extension of the
card, which a client that does not know it simply ignores:

```shell
curl -s "$A2A/.well-known/agent-card.json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '.capabilities.extensions[]
  | select(.uri == "https://choregos.dev/a2a/extensions/skill-fields/v1") | .params.skills'
```

With the CLI, a required field is marked with a `*`:

```bash
choregos a2a skills
```

**What you should see:** one skill, `billing-api/ship-a-change`, taking `ticket` (required) and
`priority`. An empty list means no workflow of a project this token can read has opted in.

### 4. Start the workflow

```shell
curl -s "$A2A" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "message/send",
  "params": {
    "message": {
      "kind": "message", "role": "user", "messageId": "order-2026-0042",
      "metadata": { "skill": "billing-api/ship-a-change", "title": "Add credit notes" },
      "parts": [
        { "kind": "text", "text": "Customers need a credit note when an invoice is refunded." },
        { "kind": "data", "data": { "ticket": "FIN-42", "priority": "high" } }
      ]
    }
  }
}'
```

With the CLI:

```bash
choregos a2a send billing-api/ship-a-change --message-id order-2026-0042 --title "Add credit notes" \
  --text "Customers need a credit note when an invoice is refunded." \
  --field ticket=FIN-42 --field priority=high
```

- The **text** becomes the work item's description, the **data** part its fields, checked against
  `metadata.inputs`. One data part at most.
- **`messageId` is your idempotency key.** Send the same message again after a timeout and you get the
  same work item back; nothing starts twice. Derive it from your own record, as here. The CLI, without
  `--message-id`, uses a digest of the message, so the same command finds the same task.
- `metadata.skill` may be left out when the card has a single skill.

**What you should see:** the task, in state `working`. Keep its `id`:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "kind": "task",
    "id": "5f0c8a52-6c3e-5f0a-9d11-3a1c7be2f001",
    "contextId": "5f0c8a52-6c3e-5f0a-9d11-3a1c7be2f001",
    "status": { "state": "working" },
    "metadata": {
      "choregos": {
        "work_item": "5f0c8a52-6c3e-5f0a-9d11-3a1c7be2f001",
        "key": "BIL-12",
        "project": "acme:billing-api",
        "state": "inbox",
        "console_url": "https://choregos.example.com/p/billing-api/items/5f0c8a52-6c3e-5f0a-9d11-3a1c7be2f001"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 5. Send a file with it

A `file` part carries its bytes in base64. Its `mimeType` must be one of the skill's `input_modes`; the
first step that lists the file's `name` in its `inputs` finds it in `.choregos/inputs/`.

```shell
curl -s "$A2A" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "message/send",
  "params": {
    "message": {
      "kind": "message", "role": "user", "messageId": "order-2026-0043",
      "metadata": { "skill": "billing-api/ship-a-change", "title": "Apply the attached specification" },
      "parts": [
        { "kind": "data", "data": { "ticket": "FIN-43" } },
        { "kind": "file", "file": { "name": "spec.pdf", "mimeType": "application/pdf", "bytes": "JVBERi0xLjcK" } }
      ]
    }
  }
}'
```
